items.title: Private equity under fire as crisis at Poundland leaves 12,000 jobs at risk before Christmas
items.summary: The crisis at Poundland has sparked fresh concern over private equity ownership of British high street brands as the budget chain teeters on the brink of collapse.
items.body:
Private equity under fire as crisis at Poundland leaves 12,000 jobs at risk before Christmas
The crisis at Poundland has sparked fresh concern over private equity ownership of British high street brands as the budget chain teeters on the brink of collapse.
Poundland, which was bought by Gordon Brothers for £1 last year, looks set to crash into administration this week, putting 600 stores and 12,000 jobs at risk in the run-up to Christmas.
Politicians and retail veterans said the demise of the company exposes a worrying trend that has seen private equity vultures prey on household names across Britain.
The row comes amid warnings that private equity has ransacked the London stock market – with figures from City broker Peel Hunt showing more than 100 UK-listed firms have been snapped up by such buyout groups in the past five years.
Gordon Brothers has rejected a rescue bid for Poundland – sparking fears it is trying to sell the group off piecemeal rather than secure its future.
Labour MP Liam Byrne, who is chairman of the business, innovation, science and trade committee, said: ‘There is this wider question of whether this is yet another bit of the British high street that has been overloaded with debt in an unsustainable way by venture capitalists.’
Poundland is nearing collapse after its owners rejected a bid for the brand
Calling on the Government to convene talks in a bid to save Poundland from collapse, he added: ‘Ministers have got to move pretty sharpish today to understand whether 12,000 British jobs are about to be sacrificed so that an American investment house can have a bumper Christmas.
‘This is three times as many jobs as British Steel that are at stake. You’ve got creditors and suppliers all depending on a rescue and you’ve got this thick layer of mystery around Poundland that we’ve got to cut through.’
Poundland, which filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators at the high court last week, closed around 200 shops as part of a sweeping restructuring under the US investment house.
The business started to rebound but Gordon Brothers put the retailer up for sale in September and has since rejected a bid that would have saved the whole company and its 600 stores.
It has fuelled concerns that the private equity firm is pushing Poundland towards administration despite receiving a bid from Martin Property Group that was backed by Poundland’s management.
The Northern Irish firm reportedly refused to meet demands for an upfront repayment of a £30million shareholder loan, which Gordon Brothers inherited from previous owners Pepco.
That means the 36-year-old retailer’s brand and its shops will not be sold as a whole, leading to a break-up of Poundland – and meaning jobs are at risk at any shop not bought.
Byrne told the BBC: ‘I’m afraid we have seen a pattern of behaviour now from private equity at Morrisons, Asda, WH Smith, Body Shop, where they’re basically geared up to the nines, overburdened with debt and its workers and high streets and consumers that end up paying the price when it all goes wrong.’
Poundland's failure would mark one of the biggest High Street collapses since Debenhams closed its doors in 2021 with the loss of 12,000 jobs.
Andy Higginson, former Poundland director, said he was ‘not entirely surprised’ by the crisis at the retailer.
He told the BBC: ‘Often particularly through the private equity cycle, good businesses can end up with bad balance sheets and that may be the case here. The situation we face is a tricky one in that the owners interests and what we the public might consider the business’ interests, can be different.’
Ministers have signalled that they are ready to take action, with the Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds last week demanding answers from Gordon Brothers and instructing officials to establish the facts.
Over the weekend, Reform UK Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick accused Gordon Brothers of ‘crony capitalism’ and called on the government to ensure Poundland ‘is not stripped for parts by its American owners’.
And Steve Smith, founder of Poundland, estimated 30,000 jobs were at risk because the retailer’s ‘suppliers will suffer or be at risk of going into administration.’
He said: ‘If Poundland goes into administration the suppliers will get next to nothing in the pound they are owed and 12,000 people will lose their jobs, the only people that will make a lot of money out of this will be the liquidators.’
The City has already sounded the alarm on the raid of listed British firms by private equity, with 131 firms taken private since 2021, according to figures from Peel Hunt.
Higginson said businesses had fallen into private equity hands as banks failed to cater to small and medium-sized firms, with the stock market ‘a shadow of its former self’.

items.title: Supermarket freezers across Europe hit by second suspected cyber-attack
items.summary: Chains in at least seven countries say fridge temperatures rose overnight in incident similar to hack of French stores Europe live – latest updates Supermarket chains in at least seven European countries have said the temperatures of refrigerators and freezers in dozens of their stores soared overnight, prompting fears of a cyber-attack similar to one that caused millions of euros of losses in France. Retailers in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Finland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden reported problems with their refrigeration systems on Monday, and several companies confirmed they had been victims of a cyberattack. Continue reading...
items.body:
Supermarket chains in at least seven European countries have said the temperatures of refrigerators and freezers in dozens of their stores soared overnight, prompting fears of a cyber-attack similar to one that caused millions of euros of losses in France.
Retailers in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Finland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden reported problems with their refrigeration systems on Monday, and several companies confirmed they had been victims of a cyberattack.
The incidents follow an attack in France last month in which hackers seized control of the cooling units in as many as 700 supermarkets, raising their temperatures as high as 50C (122F) and causing fires and food losses estimated in the tens of millions of euros.
A growing range of devices, including refrigeration systems, can now be monitored and controlled remotely, leading authorities to particularly fear government-sponsored hybrid attacks in the wake of Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
Sweden’s Coop chain told the daily Aftonbladet that six of its stores had been hit, while ICA said it was “aware that a limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems”.
An ICA store at Sjöbo in southern Sweden posted that its fridges and freezers had been hacked and their temperature set at 50C. Another in Stockholm said its freezers were broken “due to a 2am cyberattack” and that “everything was destroyed.”
The head of the national cybersecurity centre, John Billow, said it was working on incidents around Sweden. It had established the country had “quite a lot of exposed operational technology devices” that needed updating or patching, he told Reuters.
The Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize, which last month reported a similar incident to police in the Netherlands, said fridges and freezers in dozens of its supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg had been hit.
It did not specify the cause, but reporters visiting a store north-east of Brussels saw refrigerators and freezers empty and a sign reading: “Due to cyberattacks, there will be no products on the refrigerated or freezer shelves. We offer our sincere apologies.”
A company spokesperson, Sarah De Meester, said the range of fresh and frozen products was “temporarily somewhat limited” in affected stores, but that distribution centres were operating normally and there was no disruption to deliveries.
Belgium’s Le Soir newspaper reported that dozens of stores and supermarkets had been affected, including five Spar outlets, Shop & Go convenience stores attached to Q8 service stations and some smaller Proxy Delhaize mini-markets.
“We started mobilising technicians at 1am,” Stephan Moelans, the chief executive of Sabcobel, which operates Delhaize’s refrigeration systems, told the paper. “We spent all night and morning disconnecting the affected installations.”
He told the Belga news agency the incident had been a cyber-attack and that the units’ evaporators were switched to defrost mode.
The Colruyt and Intermarché supermarket chains also said they had been hit by technical problems affecting fridges in five and 15 of their stores respectively, and Carrefour Belgium reported disruption in about 15 of its 700 stores.
“It’s a cyber-attack, there is no other reason,” said Mich Vergauwen, a Carrefour spokesperson. An Ikea Belgium spokesperson likewise told Agence France-Presse that a cyber-attack had caused the temperature of freezers in its Mons store to rise suddenly.
Ikea, famous for its in-store Swedish meatballs, said it had had to remove some food products from refrigeration units as a precaution and expected some food waste as a result.
In Finland, the Helsingin Sanomat newspaper said stores operated by the Kesko supermarket chain were investigating similar problems, while the Dutch public radio NOS reported that the systems of at least 17 mainly small local stores had been affected.
At one Estonian supermarket chain, attackers accessed a computer controlling the refrigeration system and turned up the temperature to 50C, the refrigeration supply company Kitman Coldtech told the ERR broadcaster.
“This is very fresh, it happened this morning,” its chief executive, Jann Mutso, said, adding that the attack was responded to within minutes and there had been no significant damage. The Selver supermarket chain said one of its outlets had been affected.
Ireland’s third-largest supermarket chain, SuperValu, said refrigeration systems limited to a specific model in 13 of its 223 stores had been affected by a cyber-incident, and that chilled and frozen products had been removed from sale.
Many cyber-attacks involve extortion or are politically motivated and are potentially carried out by state-level actors, said Tom Hegel of the cybersecurity firm SentinelOne. But the supermarket attacks, with no financial demands, point to sabotage, he said.
“Retail is an easy target because retail chains run enormous estates of refrigeration controllers, building management systems, door access panels and point-of-sale gear,” Hegel told Reuters.
Patrick Lamplmair of the cybersecurity firm Tributech said cyber-attackers would keep going “until it stops working” because the method was “cheap and the damage is immediate”. Many refrigeration systems had knownand as yet unfixed flaws, he said.
“Thousands of these controllers were still reachable from the internet after the French attack,” he said. “A few commands to a temperature controller can destroy stock overnight and close stores.”
In the French attack, the hackers pirated controllers mostly supplied by the Danish company Danfoss, which said subsequently that it had identified some security flaws last year and had “long recommended” customers install updates.
The hackers remotely overrode the settings on thousands of freezers, fridges and chiller cabinets at chains including Intermarché, Coopérative U, Carrefour, Leclerc and Monoprix, pushing them from as low as -27C to well over 50C.
The stores had to discard vast quantities of fresh meat, dairy and frozen products. Individual supermarkets reportedly suffered losses ranging from tens of thousands of euros to more than €130,000 (£109,000).
The Paris prosecutor’s office has opened a formal investigation into the French attack and the prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, instructed France’s national cybersecurity agency, Ansii, to investigate.
The agency subsequently reported that supermarkets using controllers from two other companies had also been targeted in the attack, but authorities have not indicated who could have been behind the incidents. There have been no claims of responsibility.

items.title: Can Marks & Spencer’s TikTok star help it ‘dump the frump’?
items.summary: Marks & Spencer will face shareholders on Wednesday, with hopes of presenting a lift from its breakout social media star, Kathryn Turner, writes Felix Armstrong. Ditch the fake blood and vampire fangs: Britain’s viral Halloween costume this year featured a white shirt, a blue sweater vest and a blonde wig. Kathryn Turner, Marks & Spencer’s [...]
items.body:
Can Marks & Spencer’s TikTok star help it ‘dump the frump’?
Marks & Spencer will face shareholders on Wednesday, with hopes of presenting a lift from its breakout social media star, Kathryn Turner, writes Felix Armstrong.
Ditch the fake blood and vampire fangs: Britain’s viral Halloween costume this year featured a white shirt, a blue sweater vest and a blonde wig. Kathryn Turner, Marks & Spencer’s director of product development, has become a runaway social media star in recent months, and the retailer has quickly capitalised on her newfound Tiktok fame.
Turner, dubbed this year’s top ‘gay Halloween’ costume, has soared in popularity in recent months after taking her followers inside M&S Food’s latest products, including candyfloss-flavoured grapes and chocolate and pistachio sandwiches.
Since relaunching her social media profiles in May, Turner has garnered 281,000 followers on Instagram and a further 319,000 on TikTok, far more than the official M&S Food channel’s 270,000. She has worked at the retailer since 1995, and her breakthrough food creation was Tubby Toast, inspired by the children’s TV show Teletubbies, which first hit the shelves in 1998.
But M&S’s latest social media star, whose fans include Nigella Lawson and Ian Wright, is not alone. The retailer has encouraged its staff to grow their individual profiles online, and the company says its employees run about 600 Facebook pages and 100 TikTok accounts offering viewers the inside scoop on its products.
Richard Hyman, an independent retail analyst, said Kathryn Turner’s online profile has “clearly a very successful campaign” for the company.
M&S Food is “performing very strongly and gaining market share,” he added. “It’s always a mistake to equate social media success with commercial progress, but this will have played its part.”
The grocer notched 10.7 per cent sales growth in the four weeks to October, according to the latest NIQ data. The analytics firm attributed this boost directly to Turner’s online presence.
“M&S’ strong performance has been supported by growing social media interest in its product launches, with director of product development Kathryn Turner attracting attention on TikTok, reflecting the retailer’s ability to turn product buzz into shopper demand,” NIQ’s data experts said.
Clothing arm in need of a lift
Marks & Spencers has long been pushing to widen its Gen-Z audience after hiring Maddy Evans, formerly of Topshop, in 2023. The retailer hopes to provide more proof when it publishes its first-half results on Wednesday.
At the company’s annual general meeting this summer, chief executive Stuart Machin told shareholders that the retailer has worked hard to develop its offering for younger customers, through collaborations with influencers like Amelia Dimoldenberg, declaring that it has successfully “dumped the frump”.
The retailer celebrated its 100th anniversary in July by staging a catwalk show at London Fashion Week, in the latest sign that M&S is finally becoming cool. But Machin has reassured investors that he will not stray too far from the middle-class families which have long propped up the brand, saying his mother had reminded him its clothes were at risk of becoming “too skimpy”.
Hyman cautioned, however, that Turner’s efforts are mainly benefitting M&S’ food arm, while its clothing and home businesses are “finding life more challenging,” despite these efforts to dump the frump.
This side of the company has been slower to recover from the cyber attack which ravaged the retailer in April last year, knocking £131m from its balance sheet. Sales in food, home and beauty fell by 7.7 per cent in the year to March, while food sales jumped by seven per cent.
The retailer told shareholders in May that its non-food arm was worse hit by the “temporary pause in online trading and systems access, which disrupted stock flow and restricted availability”.
But analysts said M&S has made solid progress since last year’s cyberattack, and its share price has gained nearly 30 per cent in the last six months. As it tries to bring its clothing business up to speed with its food arm, the retailer may have benefited from a surge in sales of white shirts and blonde wigs this Halloween.

items.title: Cadbury filled eggs return in time for Easter 2027 head start
items.summary: Cadbury is urging retailers to get a head start in the run-up to Easter 2027 with the return of its filled eggs range. Brand owner Mondelēz International says seasonal sales continue to play a crucial role for convenience retailers, with 72% saying they are very… This story continues at Cadbury filled eggs return in time for Easter 2027 head start Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Brand owner Mondelēz International says seasonal sales continue to play a crucial role for convenience retailers, with 72% saying they are very important to their business.
“With Easter 2027 bringing a more compressed season, planning across the full Easter trading period is key,” the company says.
The sales opportunity taps into occasions including, self-eat, sharing, egg hunts and gifting, with Easter being the second biggest season for retail performance after Christmas, it adds.
The Cadbury filled egg range includes:
- Cadbury Creme Egg (40g, RRP 85p)
- Cadbury Biscoff Filled Egg (32g, RRP 85p)
According to Mondelēz, the average shopper buys four filled eggs across the Easter season, “emphasising the importance of strong availability and visibility in-store from the beginning of the Easter sales period in November.”
Its “How You Eat Yours” consumer campaign runs from January to March and its retailer competition “How Do You Display Yours?” is back from this month (November).
Exclusive to independent convenience retailers, the competition invites them to share their most innovative and eye-catching Cadbury Creme Egg displays for the chance to win £1,000 for the best display.
In addition, every display submitted will enter retailers into a prize draw, with one lucky retailer per month from November to February winning £1,000.
To enter the competition, retailers can visit SnackDisplay.co.uk, Mondelēz International’s trade website.
Sarah Walker, brand manager for Cadbury Creme Egg at Mondelēz International, said: “We are excited to kick off the Easter season with a Cadbury Creme Egg campaign that will look to drive footfall into stores.
“Cadbury Creme Egg is the signpost of the Easter season, and we know shoppers have their own individual ways of enjoying it.
“Our ‘Admit How You Eat Yours’ campaign really allows us to ignite the Easter conversation and bring that individuality to life in a light-hearted way.”

items.title: Poundland's former owner offers to invest as minister prepares to meet board
items.summary: Wolverhampton's Steve Smith says he attempted to contact Gordon Brothers but did not get a reply.
items.body:
Poundland's former owner offers to invest in firm
- Published
Poundland's former owner has said he would invest in the firm as a government minister said she would meet the firm's board.
Steve Smith, who founded the Walsall-based business, leaving it in 2006, said he had attempted to contact owners Gordon Brothers having been "really surprised" to learn about them filing for administration when sales were up 11% on last year.
The BBC understands that Business Minister Kate Dearden will meet with senior Poundland executives later this week to discuss the company's threatened insolvency.
US-based Gordon Brothers said it was evaluating interest for the whole business and formal and indicative offers for significant viable parts of it.
Gordon Brothers, who bought the firm from Polish retail group Pepco last year for Â£1, has stopped funding the business and rejected a takeover offer from Irish firm Martin Property Group (MPG).
The retailer has given the business until Thursday to find a rescue deal, putting up to 12,000 staff at risk.
It's understood the meeting with Deardon will be predominantly a "fact finding" meeting with government sources conceding there is limited scope for the government to intervene in a commercial transaction albeit one that puts over 10,000 jobs and hundreds of stores at risk.
The meeting was first reported by Sky News.
There is no current meeting planned between the government and executives from current owners, US private equity group Gordon Brothers.
Concerns have been raised that Gordon Brothers have declined an offer from another buyer to keep Poundland afloat in order to ensure repayment of Â£30 million loan it inherited after buying the company for Â£1.
More on Poundland
- 'Poundland closure would leave a void in our town' 
  - Published2 days ago
- How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant 
  - Published3 days ago
- Poundland staff protest after chain approach administrators 
  - Published3 days ago
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the government was "ready to support" staff as he also called for answers over why an offer to buy the business had been rejected.
Smith, from Wolverhampton and who set up the firm in 1990 with a store in Burton-upon-Trent, Staffordshire, said he contacted the owners over the last three months but had no reply. He had thought that was good news as he assumed the firm must have had offers on the table.
"And maybe I was a bit too late, but I'd certainly... with talking to the staff and how Poundland's performing at the moment, I'd certainly, if there's an opportunity, I definitely want to put some money back in there."
He said he was still in touch with staff there at levels within the business and "even last week" sales were 11.2 % upon last year.
"Although Poundland made a loss last year, they're going to make a good profit this year, so it's just crazy."
He warned that the two or three thousand suppliers to the firm only worked for Poundland so they would be directly affected by its collapse.
"This is not just about 12, 000 jobs. I'm estimating more like 20 or 30,000 jobs," he added.
The company has 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, and Smith said it had between four and five million customers a week, so with Poundland not being present on high streets would "cause a lot of other retailers to fall as well".
Liam Byrne, chair of the Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee and Labour MP for Birmingham Hodge Hill and Solihull North, said he felt the company could be saved and "the whole deal stinks to high heaven right now".
"Because I think the issue that we've got is, you've got an owner that could well be trying to cut and run, to sell a business that is in fact a going concern in order to maximize their own profits and put in jeopardy 12,000 British jobs on the high street."
'Get on the case now'
"Our message today to government and to ministers is, do not leave this to the last minute, which is Thursday... please get on the case now to get everybody around the table to maximize every option to save as much of the business as possible," he added.
In a statement, the board of Poundland Limited said it had been "working on a formal sale process for Poundland" and despite "enormous efforts it had not been possible to identify an acceptable offer for the business as a whole".
"We recognise any sale process creates uncertainty and particularly when set against a challenging UK economic environment."
Gordon Brothers said: "While Martin Property Group had been identified as the preferred bidder by Poundland's management team, attention must now turn to other active bids."
The interest, formal and indicative offers were being evaluated "with a view to minimising uncertainty for Poundland's people and all relevant stakeholders."

items.title: New Spar and BP service station for Bradford
items.summary: Valli Forecourts has opened a new Spar store and BP service station near Bradford’s busy ring road. The company, which now has 18 petrol stations and convenience stores across the north of England and Birmingham, wants the Canal Road forecourt to become one of its… This story continues at New Spar and BP service station for Bradford Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The company, which now has 18 petrol stations and convenience stores across the north of England and Birmingham, wants the Canal Road forecourt to become one of its leading sites.
Canal Road has a range of food-to-go options, with Spar’s £4.50-or-less meal deal in-store alongside a sit-in Subway and two Costa Coffee machines.
Tango Ice Blast, Coca-Cola slush and F’Real milkshakes and smoothies are also available.
The store offers all the usual convenience store services, with an area dedicated to protein products, as well as accessories and car care.
The BP forecourt includes 12 regular pumps, all with BP’s Ultimate fuel option and AdBlue dispensers, and three dedicated HGV pumps.
Five jet washes, a rollover car wash, an air, water and vacuum machine, ATM and customer parking complete the exterior facilities.
The Subway also has a drive-through hatch to the rear of the Spar store.
Adam Valli, business development manager at Valli Forecourts, said: “The team is absolutely delighted to have brought to life a superb store right in the heart of Bradford.
“The project has been in the pipeline for a while, and with the effort of the team and our local partners, we believe we have truly added something special to the community.
“We have stuck to our tried and tested format in the development of Canal Road. The site has fantastic amenities including plenty of retail pumps, HGV and AdBlue dispensers, as well as state-of-the-art car valet facilities.
“These are complemented by an excellent Spar convenience store offering with Costa Coffee and a flagship Subway store.
“The store is designed to accommodate the evolving needs of the local community as well as support through traffic.
“We have incorporated an extensive offering with special promotions running to ensure that all customers enjoy their experience when they visit Canal Road.”
The store is supplied by Spar distributor James Hall & Co.

items.title: Sixty seven per cent of shoppers will trade delivery speed for lower costs
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Retailers investing in AI ahead of Peak 2026 risk focusing on operational efficiencies while overlooking the delivery fundamentals that matter most to shoppers, according to new research from Scurri. Two studies of UK retailers and consumers show businesses accelerating their use of AI to tackle rising costs and increasingly complex customer journeys. But shoppers want […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Retailers investing in AI ahead of Peak 2026 risk focusing on operational efficiencies while overlooking the delivery fundamentals that matter most to shoppers, according to new research from Scurri.
Two studies of UK retailers and consumers show businesses accelerating their use of AI to tackle rising costs and increasingly complex customer journeys. But shoppers want to keep delivery affordable, be told when their order will arrive and get communications quickly when something goes wrong.
64% of consumers worry retailers are using AI mainly to reduce costs. Among retailers, business efficiency is one of the leading reasons for AI adoption, cited by 32%.
Yet shoppers appear less interested in the technology than the outcome. When waiting for an order, 53% say real-time tracking matters most and 44% prioritise an accurate delivery date. Almost half (47%) would accept a Peak order arriving late if they had been warned in advance.
The findings also challenge the assumption that Peak shoppers demand even faster fulfilment. Free delivery matters to 61%, compared with 29% prioritising next day delivery and just 13% same day. Two thirds (67%) would accept longer delivery times during Peak in return for free or cheaper delivery.
The Peak battleground may therefore be shifting from speed towards certainty and value. Retailers are looking to AI to help deliver this. Almost six in ten (58%) say they are likely to use automated AI to manage ecommerce delivery strategy and carrier operations, while retailers estimate AI automation of carrier management could reduce delivery costs by an average of 10.6%.
AI could also help address problems before they reach the customer; 33% of retailers see potential in predicting and preventing failed deliveries, while 31% identify monitoring delivery issues and carrier performance.
Consumers want AI but they also want control. Some 60% would be likely to use an AI agent capable of resolving a delivery problem, such as finding a parcel, rearranging delivery or organising a refund or replacement. However, 88% say they should always have the option to speak to a human and 85% want to know when they are interacting with AI. 31% do not believe AI would improve their delivery experience at all.
Rory O’Connor, Scurri founder and CEO, said, “Peak is going to provide a reality check for retail AI. Retailers understandably want AI to reduce costs and complexity, but shoppers don’t care about the technology, they want to know whether delivery is affordable, whether it arrives when promised and whether someone takes responsibility when things go wrong.”
“The opportunity is to use AI to make the delivery promise more intelligent, by selecting the right carrier, identifying potential failures before they happen and giving retailers and customers better visibility.”

items.summary: A new Nisa store has opened in Wishaw, Lanarkshire, after the operator of the site switched from his former fascia, KeyStore. The 2,000sq ft Caledonian Road store has had a full re-fit before re-launching as a Nisa, supplied by Co-op Wholesale. Mani Anwar operates the… This story continues at Nisa store opens in Lanarkshire Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The 2,000sq ft Caledonian Road store has had a full re-fit before re-launching as a Nisa, supplied by Co-op Wholesale.
Mani Anwar operates the store, which serves a residential area with everyday essentials and Co-op brand products, as well as offering food- and drink-to-go, including a Lavazza coffee station and Spud Kings baked potatoes.
Fiona Shearer, regional development manager at Co-op Wholesale, said: “This is an excellent addition to our estate and a great opportunity for Mani and the team.
“The store occupies a strong location and has all the ingredients for success, combining a modern retail offer with the convenience local shoppers are looking for.
“We look forward to supporting the team as they establish and grow the business.”
Anwar added: “Converting the store to Nisa marks an exciting new chapter for our business.

items.title: Boots brings Korea’s latest wellness trend to UK high streets
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. In a UK high street first, Boots is bringing Korean wellness innovation to customers through a dedicated K-Wellness offering, making the latest trends from Seoul more accessible than ever. The move builds on the success of K-Beauty at Boots, with Korean beauty sales delivering triple-digit year-on-year growth,1 with one K-Skincare product selling every seven seconds.2 […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
In a UK high street first, Boots is bringing Korean wellness innovation to customers through a dedicated K-Wellness offering, making the latest trends from Seoul more accessible than ever.
The move builds on the success of K-Beauty at Boots, with Korean beauty sales delivering triple-digit year-on-year growth,1 with one K-Skincare product selling every seven seconds.2 On boots.com, the category continues to attract more customers, with active shoppers up over 20% year-on-year.3
The K-Wellness launch reflects the growing influence of Korean innovation on beauty and wellness routines. Searches for ‘wellness’ on boots.com have increased by more than 200% over the past 12 months,4 underlining the growing customer demand for a blended beauty and wellbeing approach.
As part of the K-Wellness launch, Boots will exclusively introduce three trending Korean wellness brands, RIN, PrePear and Seoul Tonic, online and in over 50 stores. They will be joined by BB LAB, a leading and established brand in Korea, available on boots.com and in 200 stores this November.
The K-Wellness launch will also feature three Boots-sourced ranges, Seoul Bloom, Yongsan Wellbeing and HABI. Created in collaboration with Korean experts, the brands draw on the country’s rich heritage and expertise in wellness innovation.
Spanning ingestible beauty, traditional Korean ingredients and entirely new functional formats, the new K-Wellness ranges build on Boots’ established presence across the K-wave. With more than 40 brands already available across K-Beauty, K-Fragrance, K-Hair and K- Pharmacy, customer appetite continues to grow with searches for ‘K-Beauty’ on boots.com increasing by over 70%.5
Joe Thorley-Mitchell, director of Boots Brand, said: “Launching into the K-Wellness space represents a bold new era of wellness, both for Boots and the wider industry. Whilst the pace of innovation continues to accelerate, we’re doing the same – tapping into what we do best by bringing the latest trends straight from Seoul, at surprisingly affordable price points.
“From chia fibre jellies to collagen cool melts and popping vitamins, we’re bringing some of Korea’s most exciting products to Boots. With dedicated Wellness Zones in over 30 stores and more than 500 Health and Wellness Specialists across the UK, we’re making it easier for customers to discover the latest trends with expert support they can trust.”
Underpinning Boots’ approach to K-Wellness is Boots Ignite, an accelerator programme designed to identify, launch and scale evolving brands, including RIN, Seoul Tonic and PrePear. By connecting emerging brands with retail reach, Ignite responds to evolving consumer interest and brings new brands to market in weeks rather than months. The programme has helped bolster Boots K-Beauty offering, introducing 21 brands, including Medicube – which has seen an increase of over 20% year-on-year in searches on boots.com.6
Grace Vernon, director of international retail partnerships, Boots Ignite & Trends, said: “Social media is accelerating cultural trends, with Korea leading the way in beauty and wellness innovation. We’re seeing customers increasingly looking to this market for new products, formats and approaches and we’re excited to bring some of these latest trends to Boots, including ingestible beauty products, collagen jelly, hyaluronic acid supplements, glutathione oral dissolving films and red ginseng shots.
“At Boots, we’re looking beyond social media popularity to identify brands that bring meaningful innovation and reflect the growing connection between beauty and holistic wellbeing. K-Beauty has demonstrated how Korean innovation can influence everyday routines in the UK, and we see K-Wellness as the next chapter in that story. Our focus is on identifying what’s coming next and making these emerging innovations more accessible to our customers.”

items.title: Landsec secures UNIQLO’s first Welsh store at St David’s, Cardiff

Global apparel retailer UNIQLO today announces plans to open its first store in Wales, with UNIQLO Cardiff set to open in Autumn 2027, marking an exciting new milestone in the brand’s continued UK expansion. items.body:
Global apparel retailer UNIQLO today announces plans to open its first store in Wales, with UNIQLO Cardiff set to open in Autumn 2027, marking an exciting new milestone in the brand’s continued UK expansion.
Located within St David’s, one of the Welsh capital’s leading shopping destinations, the new store will span approximately 940 sq metres of sales floor across two floors. The opening will bring the UNIQLO store experience to Wales for the first time, offering customers in Cardiff and beyond access to the brand’s signature LifeWear collections.
Recognised for LifeWear, UNIQLO’s philosophy of creating high-quality, functional and thoughtfully designed clothing to make everyday life better, the new Cardiff store will offer a comprehensive range of products for men, women, kids and babies, bringing the brands focus on quality, comfort and functionality to customers across Wales.
Alessandro Dudech, COO of UNIQLO UK said: “We are incredibly excited to take another important step in UNIQLO’s UK expansion with the opening of our first store in Wales, in Cardiff, in Autumn 2027. Cardiff is a vibrant city with a rich cultural heritage, and with an existing base of Welsh customers already shopping with us online, we are delighted to bring the UNIQLO experience closer to them and introduce LifeWear to even more customers across Wales.”
Clare Dutton, portfolio director at Landsec, said: “UNIQLO choosing St David’s for its first store in Wales is a significant signing. The brand’s high-quality fashion and unique in-store experience has broad generational appeal and will bring something new to Cardiff’s retail offer. Having built a strong relationship with UNIQLO across our wider portfolio, we’re pleased to be welcoming the brand to St David’s as it continues its UK expansion.”
“Uniqlo’s arrival builds on the investment we’re making in St David’s and our focus on bringing new brands and experiences to the centre. With footfall continuing to grow, we’re seeing strong momentum as we look to attract more leading brands to the destination.”
UNIQLO currently operates 26 stores across the UK, with Cardiff joining Bath, Brighton, Leeds
and Canary Wharf as part of the brands continued expansion in 2027.

New digital screens, an upgraded gaming zone, hands-on […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Currys opens its new state of the art Cambridge store today, bringing tech to life through hands-on experiences and the friendly, expert advice customers expect at any Currys store.
With a fresh look and an easier-to-browse layout, the store takes the familiar Currys shop a step further. New digital screens, an upgraded gaming zone, hands-on demo areas and a purpose-built Business Hub puts customers at the heart of the design, giving them more ways to see, feel and try tech than ever before.
Just in time for the festive period, the opening weekend will feature exclusive deals, a range of activities, giving customers the chance to win great prizes, get hands-on with the latest tech, quiz our experts and discover our exclusive events calendar.
It marks the start of an ongoing programme of weekly showcases, demonstrations and experiences designed to help customers get even more from their technology. Visit the Cambridge Currys store website to find out what’s on.
Highlights include:
- Showcase and demo zones: try tech before buying, with dedicated spaces for coffee demonstrations and an enhanced gaming experience.
- Currys Business Hub: a dedicated space where local business customers can get expert advice and find the right tech for their business.
- Front-of-store event space: a flexible area for live demos, product showcases and regular events – supported by suppliers.
- Enhanced Order & Collect area: making online purchases easier to collect.
- Improved recycling points: drop off old tech in exchange for at least £5 in Currys vouchers.
- New shopping layout: designated seating areas to talk through purchases with colleagues, and new lighting and sound system.
“I’m so excited about today’s opening, and about where it takes Currys next, with our stores and online working together as one. Colleagues are at the very heart of what makes Currys special, and our stores give them a brilliant place to bring amazing technology to life, helping customers discover, experience and get the most from the latest tech. I can’t wait to welcome Cambridge customers into the new store and see them enjoying even more ways to see, feel and try the tech for themselves,” Lindsay Haselhurst, chief pperating officer, Currys.
The store will also test improvements that could be introduced elsewhere across the estate, depending on customer response and results. The retailer has relocated to this new premises a few doors along from its previous store at Cambridge Retail Park, continuing its 26th year in the city.
As one of almost 300 Currys stores across the UK&I, Cambridge combines the convenience of shopping online with expert help in person. Customers can research online, get hands-on in store or order online and collect, choosing how they shop to suit their day.

items.title: Fenwick reveals 2026 Christmas Window display in Newcastle
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. The highly anticipated 2026 Fenwick Christmas Window has officially been unveiled as The Gruffalo’s Child, bringing the much-loved children’s story by acclaimed author Dame Julia Donaldson and award-winning illustrator Axel Scheffler to life in a magical festive display, created in partnership with Macmillan Children’s Books and Magic Light Pictures. One of the nation’s most cherished […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
The highly anticipated 2026 Fenwick Christmas Window has officially been unveiled as The Gruffalo’s Child, bringing the much-loved children’s story by acclaimed author Dame Julia Donaldson and award-winning illustrator Axel Scheffler to life in a magical festive display, created in partnership with Macmillan Children’s Books and Magic Light Pictures.
One of the nation’s most cherished children’s books, The Gruffalo’s Child has captivated generations of readers with its enchanting tale of imagination, adventure and courage. This year, Fenwick has reimagined the beloved story with a festive twist, creating a magical Christmas experience that celebrates the joy of storytelling and reading together.
The spectacular window display transports visitors into the deep, dark wood, where the Gruffalo’s child embarks on a daring adventure while her father sleeps. Set against a magical snowy woodland, the story unfolds as she tiptoes through the forest in search of the mysterious Big Bad Mouse, encountering familiar characters Fox, Owl and Snake along the way.
As the adventure continues, the little mouse casts a giant shadow beneath the moonlight, frightening the Gruffalo’s child and sending her scurrying back through the snowy woodland. With Santa’s sleigh gliding through the night sky, the story takes a festive turn as she returns to her cosy home, complete with a twinkling Christmas tree, beautifully wrapped presents and a glowing fire. The display concludes with the Gruffalo’s child snuggled up beside the Gruffalo, surrounded by the warmth, wonder and magic of Christmas.
Dame Julia Donaldson, author of The Gruffalo’s Child, comments: “It’s wonderful to see The Gruffalo’s Child brought to life in such a magical way at Fenwick. The Fenwick Christmas windows are such a loved tradition in Newcastle, and I’m delighted that the story will be part of creating special memories for families this year. I also hope the windows inspire children and families to discover, or rediscover, the joy of reading together.”
Axel Scheffler, illustrator of The Gruffalo’s Child, added: “It’s a real pleasure to see the world of The Gruffalo’s Child brought to life on such a grand scale. From the snowy forest and much-loved characters to the movement within the windows, it’s wonderful to see my illustrations transformed into something so imaginative and full of life. I hope families enjoy discovering all the little details and that the windows bring plenty of smiles to children and grown-ups alike this Christmas.”
Behind the magical display is a remarkable feat of creativity and craftsmanship, with months of planning, design and production going into transforming the much-loved story into a series of animated Christmas scenes. From the intricate woodland setting and carefully crafted characters to the movement, lighting and festive finishing touches, every detail has been thoughtfully considered to capture the charm of Axel Scheffler’s illustrations and the imagination of Julia Donaldson’s storytelling.
Mia Fenwick, CEO, Fenwick, said: For generations, the unveiling of the Fenwick Christmas Window has marked the start of the festive season, bringing families together from across the North East and beyond. Bringing The Gruffalo to our windows has been a long-held ambition, and we couldn’t be more delighted to make it happen in such a special year for this much-loved character. Dame Julia Donaldson’s wonderful storytelling and Axel Scheffler’s iconic illustrations have captured the imaginations of children around the world, and we can’t wait to bring their world to life this Christmas in a celebration of the magic of storytelling.
For more than half a century, the Fenwick Christmas Window Reveal has been one of the North East’s most treasured festive traditions, bringing generations of families together on Newcastle’s Northumberland Street to mark the beginning of the Christmas season. From much-loved literary classics to enchanting festive adventures, the windows have become a cherished part of the region’s Christmas celebrations, with previous displays including 2025’s A Christmas Carol, illustrated by Chris Riddell. What began as a much-loved local tradition has grown into an event attracting national attention and, through its annual livestream, reaching audiences around the world, sharing a little of Newcastle’s Christmas magic far beyond the North East.
This year’s spectacular reveal took place on Sunday 1 November, as families and friends gathered on Northumberland Street to share in one of Newcastle’s most anticipated moments of the year. Among those invited to experience the magic were children and families from Fenwick’s partner schools, hospitals and charities, alongside lucky winners of the Christmas Window Reveal ballot. The moment was also shared with audiences further afield through a live broadcast on Fenwick’s official YouTube and Instagram channels, allowing families across the UK and beyond to join in the celebrations.
Continuing another much-loved festive collaboration, Fenwick has once again partnered with Royal Northern Sinfonia, based at The Glasshouse International Centre for Music, to create a specially recorded soundtrack for the Christmas Window.
This year’s music is a playful reimagining of Edvard Grieg’s In the Hall of the Mountain King, performed by Royal Northern Sinfonia and conducted by James Weeks. Arranged by Ian Anderson, the familiar piece has been given a festive twist, with sleigh bells and playful animal sounds woven into the music to bring the window’s story to life.
James Thomas, Executive Director, Royal Northern Sinfonia and Classical Music at The Glasshouse, said: “There’s something really special about being part of Fenwick’s Christmas Window. It’s a tradition that means so much to people across the North East, and we’re delighted that Royal Northern Sinfonia can help bring the story to life through music once again.
“Grieg’s In the Hall of the Mountain King is such a wonderfully dramatic piece, and Ian’s arrangement gives it a playful festive twist. It’s been great fun bringing all those little musical details together, and we hope families enjoy discovering them as they watch the story unfold.”
To celebrate this year’s display, an exclusive bespoke Fenwick The Gruffalo’s Child bauble will be available to purchase at Fenwick Newcastle and online at fenwick.co.uk A special keepsake to commemorate the 2026 Christmas Window, a charitable donation from sales will go to the National Literacy Trust, supporting its work to improve literacy and inspire a love of reading.
Re-watch the magical moment Fenwick’s 2026 Christmas Window was revealed on the Fenwick Official YouTube channel, and experience The Gruffalo’s Child on Northumberland Street, Newcastle, until early January 2027.

HIDE, the ambitious ready-to-eat nutrition brand, backed by Scientific Ambassador Dr Rupy Aujla and joined by co-owner Grace Beverley, is set to disrupt supermarket aisles this October with the launch of five new products across Tesco stores exclusively.
HIDE’s new Chicken Shawarma Grain Bowl, available as part of Tesco’s Premium meal deal, launches alongside an exciting new snack range featuring two delicious multipack bites and two convenient snacking trays. Together, the launch aims to make nutritious, ready-to-go food more accessible to consumers across the UK, while bringing a much-needed shake-up to the nation’s snack aisles.
The launch, which sees HIDE expand its presence into more Tesco stores as well as entering the snack category, marks another key milestone in the brand’s mission to make honest and nutritious food more accessible for all.
For too long, convenience has come at a cost, but HIDE is founded upon straightforward principles: food should taste delicious and be made from ingredients you recognise.
Dr Rupy, HIDE’s Scientific Ambassador, explains: “To put it simply, we’re making meals you can eat every day that your body will thank you for,” and that is exactly what HIDE’s new product offering aims to provide.
Upgrade your meal deal: Introducing the new Chicken Shawarma Grain Bowl with Garlic & Herb Dressing and Red Pepper Hummus
Built around whole ingredients, nutrient prioritisation, and more transparency, the new Chicken Shawarma Grain Bowl comes with tender chicken breast on a bed of Shawarma-spiced spelt and chickpeas, with a side of chilli-roasted sweet potato, citrus pickle and spinach. Topped off with a creamy garlic and herb dressing and delicious red pepper hummus.
There are no protein powders, fibre isolates or artificial flavourings. Just real food with nothing to HIDE.
Created by chefs who have cooked at BAO, Jason Atherton and Galvin, to ensure exceptional flavour and nutrition, HIDE’s new meal is built around one brilliantly simple principle: using real, recognisable ingredients you’d find in your own kitchen.
That means using real chicken, real ingredients and proper technique to ensure it hits robust nutritional guardrails”

- Tender chicken breast, Shawarma-spiced spelt, chickpeas, chilli-roasted sweet potato, citrus pickle, spinach leaves, creamy red pepper hummus and tangy garlic & herb dressing

- No artificial flavours, colours or preservatives
- Less than 5g of added sugar
- Mild
- Available as part of the Premium Tesco Meal Deal (£5.50 with Tesco Club Card, £6 without)
Nutritional Information: This salad contains 28 grams of protein, 8 grams of fibre, and 28 plants and spices for a total of 374 kcal.
HIDE takes on the snack aisle with FOUR new nutritious products, launching exclusively at Tesco
Global search demand for “on-the-go healthy snacks” has increased by 556% in the past year, and HIDE’s exciting new additions are set to fill this gap in the market.
These four game-changing snacks are flavour-first and nutrient-focused, including nothing you wouldn’t find in the kitchen cupboard. That means 100% chicken thigh. No fillers, emulsifiers, preservatives, artificial flavours or artificial colours, just tasty, honest food.
Introducing tasty new multipacks and snacking trays
Tikka Chicken Bites with Red Pepper Multipack 5 x 32g:
These bites combine chicken with red pepper, lentils, and spinach in delicious tikka spices.
Nutrition: They contain 4.5g of protein, 25 plants & spices, and 52 kcal per pack. Made with 100% chicken thigh & breast
RRP: £4 at Tesco (£3 with Tesco Clubcard – prices correct as of 14.10.26)
Jerk Chicken Bites with Sweet Potato Multipack 5 x 32g
Caribbean-inspired chicken bites with sweet potato, kale, & black turtle beans in delicious jerk seasoning.
Nutrition: These contain 4.5g of protein, 22 plants & spices, and 49 kcal per pack. Made with 100% chicken thigh & breast.
RRP: £4 at Tesco (£3 with Tesco Clubcard – prices correct as of 14.10.26)
Tikka Chicken Bites with Red Pepper and Mango & Scotch Bonnet Chutney – 230g pack snacking tray
Delicious chicken bites with red pepper, lentils, spinach, and tikka spice, with a side of sweet mango & Scotch Bonnet chutney.
Nutrition: These contain 16g of protein, 27 plants & spices, and 177 kcal per serving. Made with 100% chicken
RRP: £4.50 at Tesco (£3 with Tesco Clubcard – prices correct as of 14.10.26)
Thai Green Chicken Bites with Edamame and Coconut & Lime Dip – 230g pack snacking tray
These combine chicken with edamame, brown rice & green beans, served with a creamy coconut & lime dip.
Nutrition: Each contains 16g of protein, 18 plants & spices, and 174 kcal per serving. Made with 100%
RRP: £4.50 at Tesco (£3 with Tesco Clubcard – prices correct as of 14.10.26)
Faraz adds: “Transparency is at the heart of HIDE, yet when it comes to most snack aisles in the UK, you’ll find these principles hard to come by. Too often, consumers are left with no option but to choose snacks with long ingredient lists and unnecessary additives at the cost of convenience. These products are set to provide a much-needed alternative.”

items.title: Design Matters: understanding the art of the shop-in-shop as Sephora prepares to arrive at M&S
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. By David Wolfenden, managing director of retail design agency Ripple Retail design innovation doesn’t always require a new flagship store. The same attention to detail is essential in concessions, particularly when the brands involved also have their own standalone stores. In September, M&S announced that it will introduce Sephora concessions into 100 UK stores from […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
By David Wolfenden, managing director of retail design agency Ripple
Retail design innovation doesn’t always require a new flagship store. The same attention to detail is essential in concessions, particularly when the brands involved also have their own standalone stores.
In September, M&S announced that it will introduce Sephora concessions into 100 UK stores from spring 2027. On paper, the partnership makes considerable commercial sense. M&S has an extensive store network, an established customer base and a reputation for quality and trust. Sephora brings specialist beauty expertise, sought-after brands and a younger audience.
But bringing these two businesses together presents an interesting design challenge. Sephora needs to feel unmistakably like Sephora, while still belonging within an M&S store. Getting that balance right will be fundamental to the partnership’s success.
A new audience for M&S
M&S has been working hard to broaden its appeal, particularly among younger shoppers, and beauty presents an opportunity to accelerate that transformation. According to Worldpanel, the UK beauty market was worth £5.2 billion in the 52 weeks to July 2026, while M&S held just 1.3% of the market over the latest 12-week period. That leaves considerable room for growth.
Sephora has established a strong following among younger beauty consumers, particularly those who follow beauty trends online and want to experience products before committing to a purchase. For M&S, the opportunity extends beyond selling more make-up and skincare. Sephora could introduce an entirely new audience to its stores, including customers who might not ordinarily consider M&S for their fashion, homeware or beauty purchases. And once those customers are through the door, the wider store has an opportunity to win their attention.
A customer visiting specifically for a viral skincare product might discover M&S clothing, accessories or homeware on the same trip. Equally, an existing M&S customer could be encouraged to explore brands they would previously have bought from a specialist beauty retailer.
That crossover is what makes the partnership particularly attractive. But it won’t happen automatically. The layout, positioning and connections between departments will have a significant influence on whether customers explore beyond their original reason for visiting.
Two brands, one retail environment
The concept of a shop-in-shop is nothing new. Department stores have operated concessions for decades, allowing brands to establish their own identity within a larger retail environment. However, there is a difference between allocating space to another retailer and creating a genuinely integrated shopping experience.
Sephora has a distinctive visual identity. Its monochrome branding, strong lighting, product-led displays and opportunities to test and discover products are central to its appeal. M&S has a different visual language, generally built around considered materials, softer finishes and a more understated presentation. Neither approach is necessarily better, and each is designed to communicate something different to its customers. The challenge will be creating a clear transition between the two.
Sephora needs sufficient visual independence to deliver the experience customers associate with the brand. Its familiar black-and-white identity should be immediately recognisable, supported by dedicated fixtures, lighting and merchandising that distinguish the concession from the surrounding departments. However, creating an entirely separate environment risks making Sephora feel disconnected from the host store.
Changes in flooring, lighting and fixture heights can help define the Sephora space without relying on physical barriers. Clear sightlines and carefully positioned access points can encourage customers to move naturally between the concession and the wider M&S environment. The objective should be to create a distinct destination within the store, rather than a store that feels as though it has been dropped into another one.
Designing for discovery
Sephora’s appeal isn’t just about the brands it stocks. A significant part of the experience comes from allowing customers to browse, test products, compare shades and discover something new. That requires a different approach to merchandising from that used in many traditional retail categories.
Customers need space to explore products without feeling rushed, while testers, mirrors, consultation points and accessible displays all contribute to the experience. Specialist beauty advisers will form part of the new concessions, but their presence needs to be supported by the physical environment. Consultation areas should be easy to find, comfortable to use and positioned so that conversations can take place without obstructing shoppers moving through the space.
The concessions will also need to accommodate a combination of established favourites, emerging brands and exclusive products. That means fixtures should be designed with flexibility in mind. Beauty trends can move quickly, particularly when products gain popularity on social media. Displays need to accommodate new launches, changing ranges and promotional activity without requiring a complete redesign each time.
Making the wider store work harder
Perhaps the biggest opportunity for M&S lies in how Sephora is positioned within its existing stores. The relationship between Sephora and the surrounding departments needs to be considered carefully.
Locating concessions near fashion and accessories could create opportunities for complementary purchases. Equally, placing them along established customer routes could introduce existing M&S shoppers to the new beauty offer. The challenge is balancing visibility with the need to create a destination that feels sufficiently special.
CBRE’s 2026 Retail Generational Survey found that 34% of younger UK consumers surveyed consider store aesthetics important, while 29% value in-store events. The findings underline the importance of creating environments that offer something beyond the transaction. For M&S, the opportunity is to turn a routine shopping trip into a more engaging experience, while giving Sephora customers reasons to explore the wider store.
More than the sum of its parts
The Sephora and M&S partnership illustrated the potential for established retailers to use their physical spaces differently to attract new customers and create additional reasons to visit. The physical experience needs to deliver on the expectations customers already have of both brands.
The first concessions aren’t due to open until spring 2027, so the final design remains to be seen, but the principle is already clear: the best shop-in-shop concepts create something neither brand could achieve quite as effectively on its own. That’s where the real opportunity lies.

items.body:
Marks & Spencer has announced it is expanding the M&S Food business in the UAE with the opening of five new large format Foodhalls over the next 12 months, in partnership with long-term partner Al-Futtaim. The new destination stores will offer a full M&S Food offer outside the UK for the first time. The format is scalable, with potential for more stores in time, as M&S expands globally.
The first new M&S Foodhall will open at Dubai Festival City in December, where M&S’ franchise partner, Al-Futtaim have operated a Fashion store since 2018 – where it currently welcomes over 420,000 customers a year. At 15,327sq ft, Dubai Festival City will be the largest M&S Foodhall outside the UK, offering more than 3,500 M&S products alongside 500 new locally sourced products carefully curated for the market. Bringing together more than 200 trusted UK suppliers with local suppliers such as Let’s Eat and Domus, the store will enable customers to tick off everything on their shopping-list and complete a full weekly shop.
It will also introduce M&S flowers internationally for the first time, alongside new hospitality concepts not used by M&S before – including a Fruit Butcher – as well as tried and tested concepts that will become a first for the Middle East, such as a Sushi Counter.
Al Futtaim have operated M&S stores in the Middle East for nearly 30 years; with strong success in its Fashion business, M&S is now looking to scale its Food business, which already has an established brand awareness of 55% in the UAE**. With latest insight*** indicating the UAE Food and Grocery market is forecast to expand at a CAGR of 3.24%, M&S see growth opportunity as it continues to expand globally.
As part of M&S’ long-term commitment to delivering exceptional quality products at trusted value, M&S is also lowering prices across over half of the Foodhall in the UAE – offering the same products, at the same exceptional quality expected from M&S. The investment ensures M&S Food is more competitively priced than ever, helping families across the UAE shop more confidently, regularly, and affordably – all while enjoying exceptional quality M&S is renowned for.
Mark Lemming, managing director of International at M&S, commented: “Our purpose is to bring the best of M&S to more customers around the world. Building on the strength of our Fashion business in the Middle East, these new large format Foodhalls are an exciting opportunity to introduce more customers in the UAE to the quality, innovation and trusted value M&S Food is known for.
“By bringing a broader range of M&S Food together under one roof, we can become a bigger part of our customers’ everyday lives, giving them more choice and more reasons to shop with us more often as we continue to grow our presence in the region.”
Wassim Arabi, president, retail of Al-Futtaim commented: “Our partnership with M&S spans nearly three decades, built on a shared commitment to quality, customer trust and a deep understanding of consumers’ evolving needs. The launch of this new Foodhall is an important milestone in that journey, bringing an exciting, elevated food shopping experience to our customers. By combining M&S’s exceptional food and trusted quality with Al-Futtaim’s local market expertise and operational capabilities, we are setting a new benchmark for food retail in the UAE. We are proud to keep strengthening this longstanding partnership and look forward to what comes next.”

items.body:
A Saturday Halloween prompted a surge in store traffic, as shoppers’ adoption of ‘Spooky Season’ continues to grow, the latest data from Sensormatic Solutions, the leading global retail solutions portfolio of Johnson Controls, reveals.
Data from its ShopperTrak Analytics platform, which captures 40 billion store visits globally each year, showed that footfall on Halloween (31 Oct 2026) rose +29% year-on-year, while week-on-week it delivered a +13% boost to High Street shopper traffic.
This builds on last year, when Halloween delivered a +4.6 percent rise in footfall versus the year prior and a +3 percent boost in weekly store visits, as it continues to grow and become a key spending event in the retail calendar.  Spending forecasts suggested that this year shopper spending on Halloween would exceed £705m, a 6% rise compared to 2025.
“The timing of Halloween, which fell on a Saturday this year, would have helped retailers capitalise on the event, which continues to grow in popularity with consumers,” said Andy Sumpter, head of consulting & analytics at Sensormatic Solutions.  “Even as consumer confidence remains shaky, Halloween shoppers put aside their purchasing hesitancy to get into the spirit of ‘Spooky Season’, prompting a rise in store traffic.”
ShopperTrak’s data showed that Retail Parks saw the biggest boost, with shopper traffic rising +32% year-on-year, followed by High Streets (+30%) and Shopping Centres (+26%).  The event also saw store visits jump +36% when compared to the daily average for the prior two weeks.
“After a Halloween boost to footfall, retailers will be looking ahead to the Golden Quarter and hoping to sustain that momentum as they get into the business end of the year,” said Sumpter.   “The Black Friday weekend will once again be a key barometer of consumer mood but will also be a make-or-break start to festive shopping in full.”
Analysis in its latest ‘Christmas 2026: UK Shopper Insights’ report predicts that the Saturday after Black Friday (28 Nov 2026) will be the biggest day for Peak Trading store visits, followed by Boxing Day (26 Dec 2026) and Super Saturday, the last Saturday before Christmas (19 Dec 2026).

This means almost three-quarters of Aldi’s products […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
More than a third of Aldi products are now cheaper than they were a year ago, despite grocery prices rising across the wider market.
New figures from the supermarket reveal that 881 products are cheaper than in October 2025, while prices on a further 1,072 have remained unchanged.
This means almost three-quarters of Aldi’s products now cost the same or less than a year ago, bucking the wider trend as UK grocery inflation rose to 2.5% in the four weeks to 4 October, up from 2.3% the previous month.
Shoppers can save on everyday essentials, including 46p on Aldi’s 10 Thick Smoked Bacon Rashers (360g, now £1.79) and 30p on Grated Mature Cheddar (now £1.89), compared with October last year.
A 1kg tub of Greek Style Yogurt is also 26p cheaper at £1.49, while Mozzarella (125g) is down 14p to 55p and Red Kidney Beans cost 10p less at 39p.
The price reductions come as UK households continue to feel the pinch, with new research from Aldi revealing that more than half of Brits (56%) are concerned about the cost of their usual grocery shop rising between now and Christmas.
More than a third of Brits (37%) are also worried about their household finances over the coming months, with energy bills (36%), Christmas presents (23%) and groceries and household essentials (21%) among the costs causing the most concern.
The research also revealed how Brits are changing their shopping habits to save money. One in three (34%) have bought fewer treats or non-essential items in the past three months, while more than one in four (27%) have switched from branded products to cheaper own-label alternatives.
Julie Ashfield, Chief Commercial Officer at Aldi UK, said: “Families shouldn’t have to give up the activities, treats or hobbies they enjoy to keep their shopping bills down. Changing their supermarket rather than their lifestyle can help leave more money for those things, which is why making everyday essentials more affordable remains our priority.”
“With more than a third of our products cheaper than a year ago, customers can see the difference on the things they buy week in, week out. And importantly, our low prices are available to everyone, with no loyalty card or app needed.”
Aldi announced in September that it had invested £340 million in cutting prices on more than 1,000 products so far this year.
Aldi has been named as Which? Cheapest Supermarket for the past 11 months, and new data also shows that Aldi’s average unit price is 31% lower than its competitors.

items.title: Your catalog may already be visible to AI agents. Making it trustworthy is the next step.
items.summary: Three barriers hinder agentic optimization. Discover how AI agents evaluate products and sway shoppers.
items.body:
AI assistants are no longer a novelty. Among people who’ve tried AI-powered search, 44% now call it their primary and preferred way to search the internet, compared with 31% who prefer traditional search, McKinsey reports. For retailers, showing up in AI shopping recommendations used to feel like the finish line. It’s turning out to be closer to the starting line.
Plenty of retailers are treating agentic readiness like a technology purchase: buy the integration, flip the switch, done. That assumption is where many agentic commerce plans start to unravel.
An agentic-ready store can be found. An agentic-optimized store holds up when an AI agent checks its product data, pricing and inventory in real time. Getting there takes a handful of concrete steps your team can act on now.
Where readiness stalls before it starts
Gartner predicts more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by the end of 2027 due to escalating costs, unclear business value or inadequate risk controls. All three trace back to planning.
Measurement is a common blind spot. Only 32% of commerce organizations report fully defined AI success metrics, and just 27% report unified customer data across sales, service, marketing and commerce, according to Salesforce. Without either, it’s hard to tell whether an agentic investment is working.
Retailers also tend to overestimate the effort required. “A common misconception is that agentic commerce requires a large AI transformation before retailers can make meaningful progress,” says Abhay Singhal, co-founder of InMobi, the global technology company behind Glance, and CEO of InMobi Advertising. “In practice, much of the work starts with the commerce infrastructure they already have.”
The gains are within reach. Retailers that have launched AI-enabled experiences report conversion gains of 5% to 15%, according to BCG. “That work has immediate value,” Singhal says. “Cleaner product data and more reliable commerce systems improve how products appear across AI assistants, search, marketplaces and retailers’ own digital channels.”
Three challenges hindering your store’s agentic optimization
Chances are your store already shows up when an AI agent goes looking, thanks to automatic backend updates you didn’t have to build yourself. That gets your products noticed. It doesn’t guarantee they get picked.
A human shopper might be won over by a brand story, an aesthetic or emotional pull. An AI agent weighs structured data: price, availability and hard specifications. “Treat the agent as a new kind of customer,” Singhal says. “It doesn’t respond to branding the way a person does. It evaluates everything it can access, and inconsistencies weaken its confidence. A single wrong price can make it less likely to recommend you.”
In a Mirakl survey of seven technology and consulting partners, including Deloitte and Accenture, respondents scored retailer readiness for AI agents no higher than 4.8 out of 10 in three areas: catalog discoverability, visibility in AI-driven search and operational reliability. InMobi’s own scans tell a similar story. Of more than 8,000 retail sites run through Glance’s ReadySetAgent tool as of mid-September, the top score was 61 out of 100.
Catalog data
Adobe’s scoring of U.S. retail sites found product pages average 66% machine readability, the lowest of any page type Adobe reported on. “An AI agent can only make a useful recommendation with the information it can access and understand,” Singhal notes. “The more clearly a retailer communicates attributes such as fit, compatibility, availability and price, the better equipped the agent is to match a product to what a shopper actually needs.”
“If those details are missing or buried in unstructured copy, an agent has less to work with,” he adds. That clarity converts. In the second quarter of 2026, Shopify found that AI-referred shoppers who reached a product page converted approximately 80% better than organic-search referrals, with that advantage rising to roughly twice the conversion rate in specification-intensive categories.
Visibility and monitoring
Agent access can break without anyone noticing. Monitoring has to be ongoing, Singhal cautions, “because a website update, authentication change or platform migration can affect agent access without creating an obvious problem for a human shopper.”
Operational reliability
Even when the technical connection is live, the accuracy behind it often isn’t. Among multichannel commerce organizations, 41% report inconsistent pricing and promotions across channels, and 40% report inventory that isn’t synced in real time, according to Salesforce. “In the holidays, price and stock change hourly,” Singhal notes. “A wrong answer is worse than no answer, and the shopper blames the retailer.”
The payoff for doing the work
For the upcoming holiday season, Salesforce predicts 20% of e-commerce traffic will originate from AI chat agents.
Sucharita Kodali, vice president and principal analyst at Forrester, also expects more shoppers to try AI tools for holiday shopping. Whether that added traffic pays off depends on the answers shoppers get. “Do people feel like they found the best product or the best deal? If they get satisfactory answers, then yes, they may come back,” Kodali says.
Helping shoppers act on what agents recommend
Making product data readable and reliable improves a retailer’s chances of appearing in AI-generated recommendations. But earning a place on an agent’s shortlist is only part of the opportunity. The next challenge is helping consumers evaluate those recommendations and feel confident enough to act on them.
“Visual capabilities can make a recommendation more useful in categories such as fashion, beauty and home,” Singhal says. “Showing how a product may look on a person or within a particular setting gives the shopper information that text alone cannot provide.”
Glance’s AI personal shopper recommends products on smartphones, apps and TVs across more than 60 million U.S. devices, often before a search begins. With its Visual Dialogue feature, shoppers upload a selfie, see products on themselves in real-life settings and explore options conversationally. When they’re ready to buy, they step into the retailer’s own website.
For brands, that links discovery, consideration and conversion in a single journey, with the sale completed on their own storefront. In early U.S. trials, 40% of users tapped through to begin a shopping journey, Glance reported. “Brands that already run a product feed for Google or Meta can connect it to our agent as is,” Singhal says.
Optimizing top products for holiday shoppers
With Black Friday just weeks out, Singhal suggests beginning with a manageable set of priority items, such as a retailer’s top 200 holiday products, though the right number will vary by catalog and sales mix. From there, he says, “Sync price and stock as often as they change, publish shipping cutoffs and return policies where agents can read them and tag AI traffic before peak.”
From agentic-ready to optimized, one step at a time
Shopper behavior and agentic commerce standards are evolving fast. That makes a custom integration for every new AI channel a risky bet, since those connections change every quarter. “Own what differentiates your brand, like your product data and customer experience, and lean on shared standards and partners for the connections,” Singhal advises.
The work done now carries well past the holidays. “Retailers have spent years optimizing their stores for the way people search and browse,” Singhal concludes. “Now they also have to consider how AI agents evaluate products and how consumers make decisions with those agents’ help. The opportunity is to connect reliable product information with experiences that give people greater confidence in what they’re buying.”
