items.body:
Philip Morris Limited (PML), the affiliate of Philip Morris International (PMI) in the UK and Ireland, has launched ZYN Black Menthol 16.5mg, the newest flavour of the highest-strength nicotine pouch in the ZYN range.
The latest addition to ZYN’s highest-strength collection, Black Menthol 16.5mg responds to growing consumer demand for stronger pouches. Giving retailers more choice for experienced pouch users, Black Menthol delivers a distinct taste of peppermint with hints of eucalyptus, for an intense cooling sensation in by far the UK’s largest nicotine pouch flavour segment, the mint-flavoured pouches, representing 46% of total category volume.
PML has expanded the ZYN range at both ends of the strength spectrum to better meet the varied preferences of existing adult nicotine users. From ZYN X-Low at 1.5mg, the lowest-strength variant in the range, to the 16.5mg for seasoned pouch users seeking a higher-strength option, ZYN is uniquely positioned to offer greater choice.
Nicotine Pouches are now used by 1 in 5 UK legal-age nicotine users, and ZYN is the #1 brand for awareness amongst the 18-29 demographic. With a large pipeline of new products, ZYN continues to give retailers the support they need in key pouch segments.
Nearly half (47%) of legal-aged nicotine pouch users try a new pouch at least monthly. Given the evident rise in the pull towards the ZYN brand – with ZYN’s search demand increasing by 19pp against other pouch brands – launching a new product with the interest in a new flavour and strength combination looks to consolidate further growth in sales for both PML and retailers.
Dor Matot, head of ZYN UK and Ireland at PML, said: “Adult pouch users are increasingly looking for variety, in both flavour and strength, and we want ZYN’s range to reflect that. Black Menthol 16.5mg gives experienced users a new option in the UK’s most popular flavour segment, and gives retailers another way to meet that demand. With the Vaping Products Duty now in place, we expect more adult nicotine users to explore alternatives, and a broad, growing range means there’s a ZYN product to suit their preferences.”
ZYN Black Menthol 16.5mg is now available to stock via the PMI Open platform, and in Wholesale from the 15th of October, with Booker Wholesalers following shortly after, by the end of October.

Poundland in peril: how rampant inflation and price wars left £1 stores exposed
items.summary: With the chain on the brink of administration, its low-profile US owners face questions about their conduct ‘It was a very successful and simple proposition,” laments one former Poundland boss. With every product in the shop sold at £1, and the price in its name, its proposition to shoppers was the clearest of any UK high street chain. Now the UK’s first and biggest nationwide single-price retailer could disappear amid heavy competition and inflation that has eaten into its ability to offer bargains. Continue reading...
items.body:
‘It was a very successful and simple proposition,” laments one former Poundland boss. With every product in the shop sold at £1, and the price in its name, its proposition to shoppers was the clearest of any UK high street chain.
Now the UK’s first and biggest nationwide single-price retailer could disappear amid heavy competition and inflation that has eaten into its ability to offer bargains.
Its potential collapse has brought distress for its up to 12,000 staff in the run-up to Christmas, and as shoppers head to the chain for Halloween costumes and treats.
Meanwhile, its low-profile owners are facing questions from the prime minister over their behaviour in the week his government’s budget attempted to offer support to the high street.
Poundland’s future hangs in the balance – and not for the first time – after the 36-year-old retailer filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators at the high court on Thursday, with the advisory firm AlixPartners lined up to run the process.
The legal measure protects Poundland, which operates 600 stores, including Dealz outlets in Ireland, from the demands of creditors for 10 days while a solution to its problems is sought. However, the prospect of it avoiding mass store closures and job losses diminishes by the day as suppliers hold back on deliveries, hurting its ability to trade.
The chain’s potential demise comes after Gordon Brothers, the American restructuring specialist which bought Poundland for a nominal £1 from its previous owner in June last year, rejected a management-backed rescue bid for the whole chain by Martin Property Group.
While the Northern Irish firm is still in talks about taking on Poundland, it is understood its offer amounts to about £15m. That would pay off only half the £30m shareholder loan, the majority of which was taken on by Gordon Brothers when it bought the company. The deal would also include taking on a further, asset-backed loan worth about £90m, it is understood.
This deal has been rejected by Gordon Brothers despite Pepco, Poundland’s former owner, which holds the other £7.5m of the debt, being prepared to wait for repayment in the hope of saving the business, as first reported by Sky News.
One source who knows Poundland well said that Gordon Brothers had already taken about £10m in fees and interest out of the chain in the last year and that wanting another £30m was “egregious”. Gordon Brothers did not respond to a request for comment and has not confirmed this figure.
Gordon Brothers said earlier this week that options for the whole and parts of the business “are being thoroughly and objectively evaluated, with a view to minimising uncertainty for Poundland’s people and all relevant stakeholders”.
Sources close to the process said Gordon Brothers was unwilling to accept the Martin deal as the latest offer includes only about £7.5m up front and the rest over the next two years, leaving uncertainty for creditors, staff and suppliers.
One source said Gordon Brothers had sought bidders for the whole of Poundland but “the market had spoken” and only one little-known financial bidder with no history of running a large retail chain in the UK had come forward who might only go on to break up Poundland itself.
Instead, the restructuring specialist is understood to believe that suppliers and staff would be safer with the “trusted established retail operators” who have already put forward firm offers for parcels of outlets that amount to about half of Poundland’s stores, which could be converted to their formats.
A deal may yet be agreed with Martin over the next 10 days, especially with political pressure from Andy Burnham. On Friday, he told the Telegraph: “We want to see jobs protected. If there was a potential owner to avoid this that hasn’t been accepted, then the business secretary and I want to know why that is the case.”
For now, Gordon Brothers appears more keen on a break-up after losing faith in the likelihood of Poundland finding a route to long-term profitability amid tough times on the high street and heavy competition.
Rapid inflation on the cost of goods and labour, energy and business rates in recent years has forced Poundland to take a hit on profits and sell products for more than £1, including items for £5 or more.
In the past, Poundland removed products if it could not sell them profitably for a pound, but its choices have become more limited. High inflation – triggered first by Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and then the Middle East conflict – has exposed a business model which always appeared to have a shelf life.
In most supermarkets a two-litre bottle of milk costs over £2, a pack of KitKats is at least £1.50 and a tin of Heinz baked beans is about £1.40, according to the price comparison site Trolley. Cutting the size of Poundland has, meanwhile, reduced its scale, making it harder to get good deals from suppliers to protect margins.
Poundland has also admitted that it made mistakes in recent years, including putting its Pepco clothing ranges into stores, which proved unpopular with UK shoppers.
The expansion of cut-price chains such as Savers, The Range, B&M, The Works and Home Bargains alongside budget online rivals such as Temu, Shein and Amazon means the cheaper end of the UK retail market is now very crowded.
Meanwhile, the low-wage shoppers that make up the core of Poundland’s clientele have little spare cash for non-essentials amid rising household bills. Those with more to spare have more options in their supermarket shop, where they are increasingly locked in by loyalty-card-linked discounts.
Poundland’s pre-tax losses widened to £85.3m in the year to September 2025, from a loss of £45.4m in 2024, as sales at its outlets in the UK, Republic of Ireland and Isle of Man slid almost 12% to £1.55bn, according to accounts filed at Companies House.
In September Poundland said its revenues had returned to growth, up 3.3% at established stores in the latest three-month period, but sources said the business was not generating enough cash to pay off its loans.
US-headquartered Gordon Brothers has a long history of involvement in selling off the assets of UK high street businesses, including offloading the stock and and fittings of failed retailers such as Toys R Us.
It previously owned the British fashion brands Laura Ashley and Ben Sherman, where it oversaw the closure of their stores, and it recently bought LK Bennett, which has also closed its stores this year.
One advisory expert said Poundland’s owners had intended the buyout to be a rescue operation rather than a break-up but ultimately: “Gordon Brothers has ended up doing what Gordon Brothers do. Leopards do not change their spots.”
He said Gordon Brothers was likely to “come out looking like the worst version” of a restructuring firm. The number of stores likely not to find an immediate buyer “might not be as catastrophic as half” but it was unlikely buyers would be found for all, he added.
Poundland’s possible demise is part of a wave of consolidation of similar outlets over the past decade.
Poundworld closed its 350 stores in 2018, and Poundland bought its rival 99p Stores in 2015. Poundland then closed about 200 of its then 800 UK stores in a restructuring last year.
Poundstretcher was bought by Majestic Wine’s owner, Fortress, in 2024.
Poundland itself has a rocky history during which it has passed in and out of the hands of investment firms. Founded with one store in Burton upon Trent in 1990, the company was listed on the London Stock Exchange in 2014 at a value of about £750m by its then owner, the buyout firm Warburg Pincus.
Just two years later, Poundland agreed to a £597m takeover by Steinhoff, the South African retail conglomerate, after the British chain struggled to digest the takeover of 99p stores.
By 2018, Poundland had to seek new investment after an accounting scandal at Steinhoff and was hived off into Pepco, a company formed from Steinhoff’s European retail business. Poundland was then preparing to rejoin the London stock market when the Covid pandemic hit in 2020, scotching those plans as high streets across the UK closed down for months.
Last year, with costs rising, Pepco was looking to sell. Gordon Brothers stepped in, snapping up the struggling chain with its £1 deal. It remains unclear whether someone new will flip another coin to bet on turning Poundland around.

items.title: Poundland crisis branded 'disgraceful' as rejected bidder reattempts takeover
items.summary: Andy Street, the former managing director of John Lewis and former Mayor of the West Midlands, is the latest to criticise the handling of rescue talks - as thousands of jobs hang in the balance.
items.body:
Poundland crisis branded 'disgraceful' as rejected bidder reattempts takeover
The looming collapse of Poundland has been dubbed ‘disgraceful’ by a retail veteran as politicians demand answers from its owners.
The future of the discount retailer and its nearly 12,000 staff hangs in the balance as it prepares to call in administrators amid calls for US investment group Gordon Brothers to reconsider a rejected bid by a Northern Irish firm.
Andy Street, the former managing director of John Lewis, is the latest to criticise the handling of rescue talks.
Street, who was also Mayor of the West Midlands between 2017 and 2024, said: ‘The apparent dismantling [of the retailer] is disgraceful. Why has a viable bid been rejected in favour of breaking up the business?'
‘The owners must be called in to explain this. Poundland must be saved to protect thousands of jobs,' added Street, whose former constituency included Walsall where Poundland’s head office is.
Dismay and outrage: The Prime Minister has said he will ask questions over the 'deeply worrying' situation at retailer Poundland
His concerns echo those of the Prime Minister, who last night said he would demand answers and had instructed officials to establish the facts.
The chain, which has 600 shops, filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators from AlixPartners with the High Court on Thursday, giving the business, bought by Gordon Brothers for less than £1 last year, some breathing room for ten days to find a rescue deal.
But the Poundland brand and its shops will not be sold as a whole, leading to a carve-up of the 36-year-old retailer - and meaning jobs are at risk at any shop not bought.
Staff cuts could hit 600 shops and a distribution centre in Makerfield, Burnham's constituency in Greater Manchester, which employs around 270 workers.
Poundland's failure would mark one of the biggest High Street collapses since Debenhams closed its doors in 2021 with the loss of 12,000 jobs.
In a statement on Thursday, the board of Poundland said that the latest move would 'bring stability' and 'several established retail operators' had made bids for 'a significant' number of shops.
A spokesman said there had not been an 'acceptable offer' made for the business as a whole, even 'despite enormous efforts' in the last two months.
This comes despite unions and the retailer’s management hoping that an earlier bid from Martin Property Group would be accepted so that business could be saved.
The firm is reportedly still keen to buy the retailer and has contacted advisers AlixPartners, who are poised to handle an insolvency process, to make clear its continued interest, according to reports by Sky News.
Talks between Gordon Brothers and Martin Property Group had broken down over the repayment of a £30million loan.
> Union bosses warn of Poundland job losses before Christmas - what next for the retailer?
Burnham said: 'We want to see jobs protected. If there was a potential owner to avoid this that hasn't been accepted, then the Business Secretary [Jonathan Reynolds] and I want to know why that is the case.'
His concerns were echoed by Labour MP Liam Byrne, chair of the Commons Business and Trade Committee, who called for an urgent investigation.
MPs have also expressed concern for workers in their constituencies. Labour MP for Clapham and Brixton Hill, Bell Ribeiro-Addy MP, said: ‘The owners must engage with workers and ministers, exploring every option to save jobs and shops.’
Poundland has struggled in recent years after ‘straying from the single £1 price point that defined its core identity’ and expanding into selling clothes and frozen food, said retail expert Jonathan De Mello.
Retailers are also battling higher costs, following Government moves to hike wages and employer National Insurance contributions, while shoppers have been lured in by online giants Amazon and Temu.
Other firms thought to be hoping to buy shops include rival Poundstretcher, which is owned by US investment group Fortress, and retailers including Iceland and Lidl.
CDS Superstores, the group behind The Range, Homebase and Wilko, is also thought to be interested. The group is owned by Chris Dawson, known as Britain’s ‘Del Boy Billionaire’.
Modella Capital, which bought WH Smith on the High Street and rebranded under TG Jones, has also been rumoured to be involved in talks.
Bally Auluk, national officer for the Union of Shop, Distributive and Allied Workers, said this week has been ‘incredibly distressing’ for Poundland staff and accused Gordon Brothers of attempting to ‘jeopardise their livelihoods.’
He urged its owners to ‘reconsider and to prioritise a unified buyer’.

items.body:
In a letter to its new customers, Smiths News has addressed immediate concerns that retailers currently supplied by InPost could face two sets of carriage charges when Smiths News takes over distribution of The Sun and The Times.
The Fed has consistently raised concerns about the potential impact of dual carriage charges on independent news retailers, making it clear that retailers should not be expected to pay twice for the same distribution service.
The retail body warned that additional costs could threaten the viability of newspaper sales and accelerate the decline in the number of retail stockists.
Fed national president Hemanshu Patel said: “I am pleased that Smiths News has listened to the concerns we have consistently raised about the prospect of a second carriage charge.
“We have made it clear that this was simply not acceptable and that failing to address it could accelerate the decline in newspaper stockists and sales.
“This confirmation is therefore welcome news for independent retailers and demonstrates the importance of making sure retailers’ concerns are heard.”
Craig Etchells, the Fed’s national vice president and chair of its news operations committee, said: “This is another hurdle overcome, and for anyone in doubt, this news reconfirms that Go National will be happening. It is important that retailers have certainty as the industry prepares for these significant changes to newspaper distribution.”
While welcoming the announcement, the Fed stressed that further clarity is still needed as additional distribution agreements come into effect.
Smiths News has indicated that it will continue reviewing its charging arrangements as newspaper volumes transfer, with any potential delivery service charge expected no later than January 2028.
Brian Murphy, the Fed’s news and operations director, said: “We remain very mindful that confirmation will still be required as other contracts commence.
“The Fed will continue to engage fully with the supply chain to ensure that the interests of independent retailers are protected and that any requirement for dual carriage charges from 2028 is avoided wherever possible.”
The Go National project will see Smiths News expand its distribution network to supply thousands of additional retailers across Britain, with further agreements involving other publishers and magazine distributors expected.
Patel added: “Our First Port of Call services are open and available to discuss any concerns or questions that our members may have. We will continue to represent their interests throughout this transition and ensure their concerns are heard.”
Retailers affected by the changes are being asked to provide their business details to Smiths News by 14 November, 2026, through www.smithsnews.co.uk/register-account to help ensure a smooth transition.

The global ancient grains market is projected to reach $10.52 billion by 2032, growing at a CAGR of 37.6% (Meticulous Research, 2024). With Ocado providing a platform for […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Teff is a naturally gluten-free, planet-friendly ancient grain with a long history of cultivation in Ethiopia and now grown around the world. Despite its heritage, it remains relatively unfamiliar to many UK shoppers, presenting an opportunity for retailers to introduce new ingredients through familiar formats. Teff has also featured in Unilever’s Future 50 Foods list, reflecting wider interest in diversifying the ingredients used in the global food system.
Teffie’s latest reformulation focuses on taste and texture, creating a brownie-meets-cookie experience while retaining the brand’s wholefood-led approach. The plant-based recipes are made without brown rice syrup, refined sugar, seed oils or artificial sweeteners. The products are naturally high in fibre, gluten-free and made without the 14 major food allergens.
For Teffie, the Ocado listing is a key step in its UK growth, extending the brand’s reach beyond its existing retail partners. It also gives shoppers another way to discover ancient grain teff in a familiar, accessible format, as retailers continue to explore opportunities in the better-for-you food category.
Jessica Singh, founder and CEO of Teffie, said: “Teff has been a staple food for thousands of years, yet it’s still unfamiliar to many UK shoppers. There are so many reasons why the UK can benefit from eating more teff: it’s high in fibre, a nutrient powerhouse loved by athletes, and a drought-resilient grain. We’re proud to be at the forefront of bringing ancient grains into everyday snacking, and we want people to experience the transformative benefits of eating teff. Our reformulated products bring together wholefood ingredients and a texture that feels indulgent, staying true to what Teffie stands for: joyful, nutrient-dense food. Securing a listing with Ocado is a significant milestone for us, and an exciting step in bringing teff, and future-proof food, to more homes across the UK.”
Dr Scott Robinson PhD, nutrition advisor to Teffie, said: “Fibre is an important part of a balanced diet, yet many people in the UK are not meeting recommended intake levels. Ancient grains like teff are seeing renewed interest for exactly this reason, and everyday foods and snacks can be one opportunity to increase fibre intake.”
“Teff is a naturally gluten-free whole ancient grain with an interesting nutritional profile, and part of a wider shift back towards grains with real nutritional heritage. Using it in a convenient snack format can help introduce the ingredient to a wider audience.”
Availability:
Teffie’s reformulated Chocolate Date Brownieand Cinnamon Bunproducts will be available on Ocado from 29th October 2026, with an RRP of £12.00 for a pack of 6.
The listing builds on Teffie’s existing retail presence at Selfridges, Fortnum & Mason, Planet Organic and Holland & Barrett Online, alongside direct sales through teffie.me.
A third flavour, Chocolate Jaffa Orange, is planned for later in 2026.

items.body:
After weeks of intense observation and analysis, Emma Sleep has been voted Customer Service of the Year 2027 in the E-commerce category
The company underwent 160 mystery enquiries and a 10-week trial period to identify the best e-commerce customer service before receiving the prestigious award.
The inquiries were distributed across the contact channels, including phone, email, internet navigation, chat and social media. The participants’ customer service performance was audited and assessed over 80 criteria in areas such as availability, expertise, friendliness and response time. The entire procedure is standardised, comparable across all sectors and carried out by an independent partner.
Vasco Figueira, senior vendor manager at Emma Sleep, comments: “Support that works starts with making things easy. We’ve improved our processes so customers can find answers and sort everyday questions themselves, which frees our team to focus on the moments when someone really needs us.
“Our people, our partners and the investment behind them have kept CSAT (Customer Satisfaction Score) strong and response times ahead of our SLAs. This award is for the team, and we’ll keep making it easier for customers to get what they need.”
This recognition reflects Emma Sleep’s continued focus on making customer support more accessible and efficient.
The winners were revealed at an awards ceremony in London, bringing together the winning teams, partners and guests for an evening of recognition.

items.title: ASC UK Awards 2026 celebrate champions driving positive change in farmed seafood
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC) has celebrated the businesses helping to drive positive change in farmed seafood at the MSC and ASC UK Awards 2026, held this week (Wednesday 28 October) at London’s historic Fishmongers’ Hall. From pioneering salmon farmers and innovative seafood brands to retailers and suppliers making ASC-certified seafood more accessible, this year’s winners […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC) has celebrated the businesses helping to drive positive change in farmed seafood at the MSC and ASC UK Awards 2026, held this week (Wednesday 28 October) at London’s historic Fishmongers’ Hall.
From pioneering salmon farmers and innovative seafood brands to retailers and suppliers making ASC-certified seafood more accessible, this year’s winners demonstrate the commitment and collaboration helping to advance environmental and social responsibility across the aquaculture sector.
Sainsbury’s continued its winning streak, securing ASC Supermarket of the Year for the fifth consecutive year, while MOWI celebrated a double victory, taking home both Farmer of the Year and Brand of the Year. Co-op was named Newcomer of the Year, Waitrose won the consumer-voted Product of the Year, and New England Seafood secured Supplier of the Year.
Maud van den Haspel, ASC General Manager, UK & Benelux, said, “These awards highlight just how important every part of the supply chain is in driving progress in aquaculture. Farmers investing in certification need strong market demand, while retailers and brands need committed suppliers to deliver on their sourcing ambitions.
“What we’re celebrating this year is that connection in action. From long-established partnerships to ambitious new commitments, our winners are demonstrating how businesses can work together to grow the market for ASC-certified seafood while supporting better environmental and social practices in farming.”
Its journey with ASC spans more than a decade, beginning with Scotland’s first ASC-certified salmon farm in 2015. Today, MOWI has more than 30 ASC-certified farms in Scotland, demonstrating its sustained commitment to meeting ASC’s environmental and social requirements.
The Brand of the Year award also recognises MOWI’s investment in making ASC-certified seafood more visible and accessible. With 100% of its branded products carrying the ASC sustainability label, MOWI has worked across retail, digital communications and chef education to build consumer awareness and understanding of certification.
Ben Hadfield, COO Scotland, Ireland, The Faroes and Canada East with MOWI, said, “Certification is an important part of how we demonstrate our commitment to our farming practices, and maintaining it across a growing number of farms takes considerable teamwork and investment. At the same time, we’ve focused on making ASC certification a visible part of our brand, helping customers understand the high standards behind the salmon they buy.
“Winning both awards is particularly rewarding because it recognises these two sides of our business and the people who make them possible.”
Alison Hutchins, ASC Producer Engagement Director, commented, “Achieving and maintaining ASC certification requires ongoing commitment from farmers and their teams. MOWI’s journey, from Scotland’s first ASC-certified salmon farm to more than 30 certified farms today, shows the value of taking a long-term approach.
“What’s equally important is the role that market demand plays in supporting that commitment. MOWI’s success in both farming and branding demonstrates how certification can connect the work happening on farms with the expectations of seafood buyers and consumers. It’s encouraging to see that recognised through two awards.”
Sainsbury’s was named ASC Supermarket of the Year for the fifth consecutive year, recognising its sustained commitment to making ASC-certified farmed seafood widely available to customers, both in-store and online.
The award reflects the continued efforts of Sainsbury’s teams and supply chain partners to maintain and expand access to certified farmed seafood.
Dave Parker, Head of Aquaculture and Fisheries at Sainsbury’s, said, “Making ASC-certified seafood part of our everyday offer requires close collaboration with our suppliers and a consistent approach to sourcing. We’re proud of the relationships we’ve built and the progress we’ve made in giving customers access to certified farmed seafood.
“Receiving this award for a fifth consecutive year is a great achievement, but our focus remains on continuing that work and building on the progress we’ve made.”
Co-op took home the ASC Newcomer of the Year award in recognition of its commitment to introduce ASC labelling across 100% of its own-brand farmed seafood range by 2027.
With work already underway towards this target, Co-op is helping to expand the availability of ASC-labelled seafood and giving more shoppers access to products from farms independently certified against ASC’s environmental and social requirements.
Sam Darley, Fisheries and Aquaculture Manager at Co-op said, “Our ambition to introduce ASC labelling across our entire own-brand farmed seafood range by 2027 is part of our longstanding commitment to responsible seafood sourcing. The move requires collaboration right across our supply chain, and we’re pleased to be recognised as Newcomer of the Year.”
Waitrose’s Organic Kefalonian Sea Bass Fillets were crowned ASC Product of the Year following a public vote that attracted more than 1,000 participants.
Receiving 301 votes, the winning product highlights consumer enthusiasm for ASC-certified farmed seafood and demonstrates how retailers can bring certified products to shoppers through appealing product ranges.
Katie Keay, Senior Aquaculture and Fisheries Manager at Waitrose, said, “We are committed to providing our food loving customers with delicious, high-quality seafood which has been responsibly sourced. Our Organic Kefalonian Sea Bass Fillets bring those qualities together, so we’re thrilled that they’ve proved so popular in the public vote.
“This recognition shows the opportunity for retailers to make certified farmed seafood an appealing and accessible choice for shoppers.”
New England Seafood was named ASC Supplier of the Year, recognising its important contribution to bringing ASC-certified seafood to the UK retail market.
The company was nominated and selected for the award by UK retailers, demonstrating the strength of its customer relationships and the value of its partnerships across the seafood supply chain.
Cassie Leisk, planet and peopledirector with New England Seafood said, “As a supplier, our role is to connect the commitment of certified farmers with the needs of UK retailers, helping make ASC-certified seafood a commercially successful part of their ranges.
“To receive this recognition directly from our retail partners is especially meaningful. It demonstrates the importance of trust, collaboration and shared ambition in developing the market for certified seafood.”
The awards brought together more than 150 guests from across the UK seafood industry to celebrate achievements in certified wild-caught and farmed seafood.
ASC also honoured Su Cox, comms and business development drector at Bakkafrost Scotland, with its Lifetime Achievement Award, recognising more than 35 years of extraordinary leadership in the Scottish salmon sector and her contribution to the industry’s long-term future.
Together, this year’s ASC winners demonstrate the breadth of commitment across the sector, from certification and ongoing improvements at farm level to stronger supply chain partnerships and greater consumer awareness of ASC-certified seafood.
This year’s ASC UK trophies are made from discarded fishing nets recovered from UK beaches – with the plastic in each one fully traceable back to the beach where it was collected.
They’re made by Ecotribo, who reinvest all the money from products made using recovered nets back into beach cleans. And with a QR code on each trophy, our winners will be able to discover the story behind the material in their award.

The agreement will see the brand expand its presence across the North of England and southern Scotland, building on […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Black Sheep Coffee (www.blacksheepcoffee.co.uk) is accelerating its UK expansion with a new franchise development agreement securing a minimum of 20 new stores across West Yorkshire and the Northern Counties, including Northumberland, Cumbria and Dumfries and Galloway.
The agreement will see the brand expand its presence across the North of England and southern Scotland, building on its existing estate and bringing its specialty-grade coffee, food and drinks offering to new audiences across the region. The roll-out is expected to create around 300 jobs over the next 5 years.
The stores will be opened by SUR Group, Black Sheep Coffee’s largest franchise partner by store numbers. The Glasgow-based group joined the network in May 2024 and now operates seven Black Sheep Coffee stores across West Scotland, including Glasgow and Ayr.
The new agreement represents a significant opportunity to build on this success, while further strengthening SUR Group’s partnership with Black Sheep Coffee. The additional territory will complement the brand’s two existing stores in Leeds and extend its reach into communities where customers may not yet have experienced the brand.
The new stores will be considered across a range of formats and locations, including high streets, retail parks and drive-thrus. This flexible approach will allow Black Sheep Coffee to reach customers in a variety of settings, making its offering more accessible both to existing customers and those discovering the brand for the first time.
Gabriel Shohet and Eirik Holth, co-founders of Black Sheep Coffee, said: “We’re thrilled to build on our presence in Leeds and bring Black Sheep Coffee to even more communities across the North through the opening of at least 20 new stores.
SUR Group has been a brilliant franchise partner in Glasgow and Ayr, with a real understanding of what makes Black Sheep distinctive – from our specialty-grade coffee and wider menu to the experience we create in every store.”
Suhail Rehman, multi brand franchise partner at SUR Group, said: “We’re proud to be growing our partnership with Black Sheep Coffee. Having seen the brand’s potential first-hand, we’re excited to take it into new territories and bring the Black Sheep Coffee experience to more customers.”
Tariq Din, business development director at SUR Group, who will lead the roll-out, said: “We’ve spent the last couple of years learning what makes a Black Sheep store work: the right product, the right location and above all, the right team providing a great customer experience. We’ll be looking at everything from high streets to drive-thrus, and we want to hear from landlords with access to high footfall locations.”
The expansion will bring Black Sheep Coffee’s specialty-grade 100% Robusta coffee, alongside its Arabica range, matcha, food, cold drinks and distinctive store designs to more communities across the region.

items.title: Britain’s blighted high streets will improve by next election, says Rayner
items.summary: Housing secretary says Labour wants to reverse fortunes of towns plagued by boarded-up shops and rogue businesses Angela Rayner has said voters will begin to see a difference in their high street before the next general election as Labour prioritises investment in struggling local communities. The housing secretary said the government had made it a top priority before the country goes to the polls to begin turning around the fortunes of places blighted by boarded-up shops and rogue businesses. Continue reading...
items.body:
Angela Rayner has said voters will begin to see a difference in their high street before the next general election as Labour prioritises investment in struggling local communities.
The housing secretary said the government had made it a top priority before the country goes to the polls to begin turning around the fortunes of places blighted by boarded-up shops and rogue businesses.
“There’s been a real sense of decline,” she said. “People see it as part of the identity of their town and area, and that’s why we’ve got our high streets strategy.”
Speaking after John Healey, the chancellor, earmarked more than £1bn in his debut budget on Wednesday to support retail, hospitality and leisure businesses, Rayner signalled that the government stood ready to take further action.
“The chancellor has shown he’s backing our high streets, backing our businesses that have been struggling and giving them the breathing space,” she said. “And he’s going to continue with that.”
In an interview for the Guardian’s series on the fortunes of Britain’s towns, Rayner insisted that the budget was “moving the needle” for the economy as she sought to defend Healey from criticism.
On Thursday the chancellor was warned by the Resolution Foundation and the Institute for Fiscal Studies that his measures were poorly targeted and had paved the way for a “brutal” spending review next year.
Meanwhile, the owners of Poundland filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, putting up to 12,000 jobs at risk in a blow for towns across the country where the discount chain is a high street fixture.
Speaking before that announcement, Rayner said the government was taking action to ease the pressure on businesses and households amid the damage to Britain’s economy from the Middle East war.
“All these businesses that people value, that make up a thriving high street, the chancellor is really giving them support,” she said.
Asked whether voters would be able to see a difference in their local shopping districts before the next general election, she said: “The money will start to come through. Already we’ve put the £5.8bn in.
“Next year, from April, business rates [cuts] will apply and you’ll see [other] money in more areas.”
On his way to becoming prime minister, Andy Burnham pledged a new dawn for Britain’s high streets, placing the revival of overlooked town centres at the heart of his agenda for government.
In response to this agenda, Healey said he would cut business rates for retail, hospitality and leisure companies in a plan worth £1bn over two years, with the relief partly funded by higher taxes on gambling and vape shops.
Labour also launched a revamped “hope on the high street” strategy alongside the chancellor’s budget to coordinate investment and the transfer of power to local leaders. This includes the already announced £5.8bn “pride in place” programme to support regeneration projects and £210m fund to transform derelict buildings.
“There’s a lot of money and funding pots going into the high street, as well as work in the public realm to deliver services and housing,” Rayner said.
However, business leaders said more fundamental changes to the business rates system were needed, highlighting that Labour had promised to replace it entirely in its manifesto.
Before the budget Andy Haldane, the former Bank of England chief economist, told the Guardian that changes to tax online sales at higher rates than in-store purchases were needed to help “level the playing field” for struggling bricks-and-mortar stores.
Hinting at further changes to come, budget documents show ministers are exploring “how the business rates system could better target online retailers in ways that minimise any indirect impacts for wider retail businesses” to fund support for the high street.

items.body:
On the back of one of its most successful UK store openings to date in Hull this month, JYSK today announces the opening of its debut store in Wales set for early 2027. The Danish retailer will be introducing its Scandinavian homeware presence to the second largest city in Wales marking a major milestone in its UK growth.
Due to open in Spring 2027, the new Swansea store located at Parc Tawe North Retail Park will provide shoppers with over 1000m2 of interior shopping heaven with JYSK’s extension product portfolio on full display.
Opening in Wales represents a significant step forward for JYSK, with the retailer entering a new UK nation for the first time since launching in England in 2008. The expansion reflects JYSK’s continued investment in bringing its affordable Scandinavian home furnishing concept to more customers across the country, with more Welsh stores on the horizon throughout 2027.
Ciaron Hearns, brand & marketing manager, UK & Ireland at JYSK, says: “We’re incredibly excited to be opening our first store in Wales and finally sharing the news after working towards this opening for some time. We’re not only opening a new store but also entering a new country with excellent growth potential. This is an important milestone for JYSK as we look to continue our UK expansion over the coming years. We can’t wait to welcome new customers through the doors and become part of the local community.”
The Swansea store will feature JYSK’s latest retail concept, designed to create a bright and inspiring shopping environment that makes it easy for customers to explore and shop. The layout will showcase key home categories including furniture, mattresses, home decor, storage solutions and outdoor living, all presented with a focus on quality and affordable value.
The opening will create over 10 new jobs in Swansea, supporting local employment as part of JYSK’s continued investment in its UK store network. The store will launch with JYSK’s usual opening-day flair, including exclusive offers, a DJ on site and additional initiatives to help bring the community together in celebration.

items.title: Post Office welcomes announcement of new government investment
items.summary: The Post Office's expansion of multi-carrier self-service Drop Boxes and modernisation of 600 branches was this week officially highlighted as part of the government's Budget strategy to champion high streets and support local postmasters. Welcoming the announcements, Neil Brocklehurst, chief executive, Post Office, said: “It’s… This story continues at Post Office welcomes announcement of new government investment Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Welcoming the announcements, Neil Brocklehurst, chief executive, Post Office, said: “It’s clear that the government continues to back the Post Office network – both through the Budget and its new strategy to champion the UK’s high streets.
“As part of his Budget, the chancellor announced that Post Office is upgrading 600 branches and aiming to roll out up to 1,000 new multi-carrier self-service Drop Boxes by the end of the financial year.
“Postmasters will now have the opportunity to bring the new technology into their branches, reducing their costs and giving customers greater choice and flexibility.
“Together with the expansion of Post Office Plus, highlighted in the high street strategy, this investment will strengthen the role our branches play at the heart of communities across the country.
“Our modernised branches will offer customers greater convenience and create new opportunities for growth in every postcode by supporting the services that local businesses rely on.
“The additional business rates support announced today for small businesses is also welcome news. Business rates relief for post offices is something that we have been campaigning for, on behalf of our postmasters. This is a first step in the right direction and we will continue our conversations on further rates support for post offices.
“These measures will help secure the future of the Post Office network, and we look forward to working with government to support high streets across the UK.”
The Post Office has also announced the appointment of Mark Freedman as its new chief financial officer. Freedman, most recently chief financial officer at Travelex, was previously group financial controller at the London Stock Exchange and UK chief financial officer at Deutsche Bank.
Freedman posted on LinkedIn: “I’m thrilled and honoured to share that I will be joining the Post Office as Chief Financial Officer this November.
“The Post Office is a truly historic institution and a vital part of the nation’s infrastructure, serving as a lifeline for communities and delivering essential services to millions of people every day.
“I can’t wait to get started!”

items.title: ACS welcomes government plans to tackle dodgy shops
items.summary: The Association of Convenience Stores (ACS) has welcomed the publication of a new report from the government, setting out six pillars of successful high streets and a commitment to root out organised crime. The Hope on the High Street report, published this week by the… This story continues at ACS welcomes government plans to tackle dodgy shops Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The Hope on the High Street report, published this week by the Ministry for Housing, Communities and Local Government, cites figures from ACS’ 2026 Community Barometer on the factors that affect people’s perception of their local high street:
‘Too many empty units is the most commonly cited factor making high streets worse (63%), while cleanliness and improved range and quality of shops are among the main things people say make them better.’ (Hope on the High Street, p54).
The report identifies six pillars of successful high streets, which are:
- Active leadership and management – reasons to have confidence
- Strong businesses, anchors and amenities – reasons to visit
- Vibrant culture, leisure, hospitality and entertainment – reasons to get together
- Easy access and connectivity – reasons to explore
- Safe, clean and welcoming – reasons to return
- A place to call home – reasons to move in
On organised crime, the report states that ‘legitimate businesses are the engine of successful high streets, creating jobs, services and places people want to spend time. But in some places the legitimate economy is increasingly being undermined by organised crime.
Criminally controlled businesses are used to launder illicit funds, evade tax, exploit workers and sell illegal goods.’
Action from the government to tackle organised crime includes:
- The Insolvency Service, Companies House and HMRC are working in partnership to identify and act against directors who use successive companies to avoid debts and sanctions
- Making it harder for criminal enterprises to set up on the high street. This includes exploring approaches taken by other countries and the role of landlords
- New training to help front-line staff in Trading Standards tackle organised crime and protect legitimate business is now being rolled out with a view to extending this to other agencies going forward
- Alongside the Tobacco and Vapes Act, the government is investing up to £30 million of new funding for enforcement agencies annually until 2028/29, including Trading Standards, Border Force and HMRC, to tackle the illicit and underage sale of tobacco and vapes, supporting the implementation of the Act.
- Prioritising activity across government to take a targeted and coordinated approach to intervening with prolific offenders, supporting policing and local partners to reduce persistent offending and improve safety on high streets and in communities.
ACS chief executive Ed Woodall said: “We can only revitalise our high streets if they are safe places for people to shop, work and invest. It is absolutely right that the Government has put safety at the heart of its new high streets strategy.
“Cracking down on rogue traders and tackling the shop theft that blights communities and undermines legitimate businesses are essential steps towards restoring confidence in our high streets and helping them thrive.”
Figures from the ACS Crime Report 2026 show that 85% of independent retailers have seen an increase in illicit activity in their area over the last year.

items.title: Healey’s business rate tweaks won’t stop ‘hollowing out’ high street, business group warns
items.summary: John Healey’s changes to high street business rates are a “sticking plaster” that will not reverse the “hollowing out” of town centres across the country, the boss of Britain’s largest business group has warned. In his maiden Budget this week, the Chancellor said he would lift the threshold at which small firms receive business rates [...]
items.body:
Healey’s business rate tweaks won’t stop ‘hollowing out’ high street, business group warns
John Healey’s changes to high street business rates are a “sticking plaster” that will not reverse the “hollowing out” of town centres across the country, the boss of Britain’s largest business group has warned.
In his maiden Budget this week, the Chancellor said he would lift the threshold at which small firms receive business rates relief from £12,000 to £18,000, exempting some 70,000 more companies from the tax. He also said he would freeze business rates bills for all other retail, hospitality and leisure firms.
The move, funded by a tax raid on gambling firms and a VAT crackdown on e-commerce platforms, will “help provide the funding for our pubs, cafes and shops to thrive,” the Chancellor said.
But the decision has come under fire from some of the country’s biggest business bodies who have criticised the government’s failure to reform the underlying business rates system. A firm’s business rates bill is calculated using the annual rental value of its premises.
Labour pledged to reform the business rates system in its 2024 election manifesto but has so far made no headway on the plans.
Shevaun Haviland, the boss of the British Chambers of Commerce, told City AM the Chancellor’s move was welcome but would do little to solve the crisis engulfing British high streets.
“It’s another sticking plaster, really. It’s another tweaking of a system that’s already incredibly complicated and acts as another tax on businesses before they’ve sold a single thing,” she said in an interview.
“It is the thing that is hollowing out our high streets. From speaking to our members it’s generally the thing they can’t pay anymore, and then they [close].”
The British Retail Consortium (BRC), which represents some of the retail industry’s biggest names, including Tesco, Sainsbury’s and Marks & Spencer, dubbed Healey’s policies a “smoke and mirrors announcement”.
Though the Chancellor said business rates would be “frozen” for the retail, hospitality and leisure industries they are still set to rise by 3.5 per cent next year, in line with inflation, meaning the high street will be saddled with extra £250m in business rates bills next April.
‘Tsunami of costs’
Haviland’s comments will add to pressure on Healey after his maiden Budget came under fire from several independent think tanks for failing to meet the scale of the crisis facing the British economy.
The Chancellor set out some £6bn of giveaways designed to give “breathing space” to households and businesses. But the statement was accompanied by a gloomy fiscal outlook from the Office for Budget Responsibility which slashed growth forecasts from 1.6 per cent to one per cent next year and raised average inflation projections to 3.4 per cent. Unemployment is also set to peak at a higher level than previously expected.
Haviland said that the cost of employing staff remained the primary concern for the Chambers’ 50,000 members.
“Our businesses want to employ young people – those million young people, not in education, employment and training. We want to employ them, but at the moment, we just can’t,” she said, adding that firms were drawing under a “tsunami of costs”.
Rachel Reeves’s decision to hike national insurance contributions for employers has ramped up the cost of taking on new staff.
Haviland said energy was also becoming a key concern for her members as the Iran war chokes off fuel supplies and pushes up bills. While households were given a £100 support package yesterday, businesses were given nothing to help soften the blow of rising prices.
“Businesses are already seeing their bills tick up, and there’s nowhere to go,” she said. “There’s literally nowhere to go. You can’t pass on these costs.”
The government was approached for comment.

items.title: Tesco retreats from Europe with £1bn sale of Czech and Slovak divisions
items.summary: Tesco has agreed to sell its businesses in the Czech Republic and Slovakia to a Dutch supermarket giant in a billion-pound deal. The UK’s largest grocer said today it would sell its operations in the two European countries to Ahold Delhaize for €1.2bn (£1bn), in what marks the company’s latest retreat from the global expansion [...]
items.body:
Tesco retreats from Europe with £1bn sale of Czech and Slovak divisions
Tesco has agreed to sell its businesses in the Czech Republic and Slovakia to a Dutch supermarket giant in a billion-pound deal.
The UK’s largest grocer said today it would sell its operations in the two European countries to Ahold Delhaize for €1.2bn (£1bn), in what marks the company’s latest retreat from the global expansion it had pursued in recent decades.
Tesco chief executive Ken Murphy said the move would help the supermarket chain to ramp up its focus on the UK market, where grocers are battling to keep prices down in the face of rising energy and supply chain costs.
Murphy said: “It has been a privilege to serve customers and invest in colleagues, stores and supply chain in the Czech Republic and Slovakia and we are proud of what has been achieved over the past 30 years.
“For Tesco, the transaction will further simplify the Group, increasing our focus on our core UK and Irish businesses and supporting our continued investment in our food-first retail ecosystem and the capabilities that will drive future growth, while enabling a further return of capital to shareholders.”
Ahold Delhaize, which owns 17 supermarket brands including Albert Heijn in the Netherlands and Food Lion in the US, will take control of Tesco’s Czech and Slovak stores in the second half of next year.
Tesco winds down global reach
In the last year, Tesco’s operations in these two countries produced £2.9bn in sales and most of the £115m operating profit generated by its “central Europe” arms. The group has 184 stores in the Czech Republic and 179 in Slovakia.
The supermarket giant operates a further 198 locations in Hungary, and reports earlier this year suggested it was seeking a buyer for this business too. But Tesco said on Friday: “Hungary is not part of today’s agreement and continues to be owned and operated by Tesco. We will continue to review all options for the future of our business in Hungary.”
Frans Muller, chief executive of Ahold Delhaize, said: “This acquisition is an important step in strengthening our position in the Central and Southeastern European region.
“It brings together highly complementary businesses with strong local market expertise and gives us the opportunity to expand into Slovakia, an attractive adjacent market.”
Analysts at stock broker RBC said: “We think that much of [Tesco’s] value has been in the UK&I business in recent years, and central Europe has had its challenges and hence we are encouraged by the reduced exposure there.”
Tesco’s exit from the Czech Republic and Slovakia follows a number of similar retreats in recent decades. The group has already withdrawn from France, Japan, Malaysia, Poland, South Korea, Thailand, Turkey and America.
The supermarket quit its US experiment in 2013, selling off all remaining Fresh & Easy stores, and the accounting scandal that nearly sunk the firm accelerated its turun inwards in 2014. Tesco’s Thai and Malaysian operations were sold for £8bn in 2020.
This moves have unwound the ambitious expansion plan set out by former Tesco chief executive Sir Terry Leahy, who said in 2007 that the group was looking to expand “everywhere”. He had said: “We are on the threshold of becoming one of the few successful international retailers. There’s plenty to do.”
The group’s European division accounted for £4.5bn of its £66.6bn total revenue last year and was recently described by Murphy as an “integral part of the group”.
Shares in Tesco gained one per cent in early trading, to 536p.

items.title: How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant
items.summary: The retail giant - which started life at a Wolverhampton market - is now at threat of collapse.
items.body:
How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant
- Published
"When I told people what I wanted to do, open shops on the high street selling things for one pound, they said, 'how will you find products to sell for a pound, what about inflation, it will never work.'"
That is how Steve Smith, the founder of Poundland, describes the genesis of the budget giant - which went on to employ thousands of people and see over a million customers a week - on his own website, external.
But now the West Midlands-based retailer is teetering on the edge, after its US-based owners Gordon Brothers cut off a vital funding supply and rejected a takeover offer from Irish firm Martin Property Group.
- Poundland staff protest after chain approach administrators 
  - Published3 days ago
- Burnham 'ready to support' Poundland staff as retailer faces collapse 
  - Published3 days ago
- The curious case of why Poundland is struggling during a cost-of-living crisis 
  - Published21 November 2025
Having spent time on his parents stall since the age of two Wolverhampton-born businessman Smith started out in the very same place - selling items for Â£1 from his own stall.
After a Â£50,000 loan from his parents he opened the first Poundland shop, in The Octagon Shopping Centre in Burton-upon-Trent, Staffordshire, on 13 December 1990.
That first day, with a range of 624 products, the store took more than Â£13,000 - "and Poundland was born," Smith said.
Smith and his wife, Tracy, now based in Shropshire, owned the company for 16 years.
In 2006, he decided the time had come and he sold his final shares in the business for Â£250m, but later said the sale felt it was "as though somebody had died".
But by 2025, the Walsall-based company was itself sold for just Â£1.
Its owner, Polish firm Pepco, confirmed it had sold the brand for a "nominal" sum to US investment firm Gordon Brothers.
At the time Poundland had more than 800 stores across the UK and Ireland and employed around 16,000 staff.
"I did pick up the phone when I heard it was for sale but I was a bit too late," Smith said after the sale.
Now, the retailer's bosses have filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which will give the business 10 days to find a rescue deal.
A protest was held outside the Poundland HQ on Thursday, Claire Sutcliffe - who has been at the company for nearly a decade - among those demonstrating.
Questioned about how she felt, the 49-year-old replied she was "very sad", adding: "Nine years is a lot working for Poundland and they've been really good to me as a Poundland family, really supportive."
Sutcliffe added that some had worked for the business for 20 years and "it's just very sad for us all".
Asked what her message was to owners Gordon Brothers, she replied: "Please just sell.
"Save our jobs, we've all got families to feed and it's... near Christmas."
Professor Sarah Montano, a retail expert from the University of Birmingham, said: "The real problem for Poundland is, when they first started it was really great because everything was Â£1, that was a really unique selling point for them.
"[Today] there's competitors which are offering very similar prices and for quite a lot of products they're offering them cheaper."
She added that some competitors had "really got their finger on the key trends".
In a statement, the board of Poundland Limited said it had been "working on a formal sale process for Poundland" and despite "enormous efforts it has not been possible to identify an acceptable offer for the business as a whole".
"The process has however attracted several established retail operators who have made formal offers, collectively these cover a significant part of the business, and we believe offer the best available prospects for shareholders, creditors and to preserve jobs," they said.
"We recognise any sale process creates uncertainty and particularly when set against a challenging UK economic environment."
They also thanked "staff, suppliers and customers for their continued support".

items.title: B&Q brings Google’s latest AI powered technology to retailer's onsite search experience
items.summary: Kingfisher owned UK home improvement and garden retailer B&Q has gone live with Google AI Commerce Search on its online store.In a LinkedIn post, Chris Swann, Digital Optimisation Lead at B&Q, said: "This brings Google’s latest AI powered technology to our onsite search experience."﻿He added
items.body:
Kingfisher owned UK home improvement and garden retailer B&Q has gone live with Google AI Commerce Search on its online store.
In a LinkedIn post, Chris Swann, Digital Optimisation Lead at B&Q, said: "This brings Google’s latest AI powered technology to our onsite search experience."
He added: "We're leveraging Google’s expertise in search, AI and machine learning to understand language, customer intent and product relevance, combined with our customer behaviour data to determine the most relevant products for every search. Continually optimising, personalising and reducing the need for manual intervention."
On demand delivery
B&Q is ramping up its fast delivery push with the launch of TradePoint Express, a same-day delivery service exclusively for trade customers, in partnership with Gophr.
The retailer has also expanded its Deliveroo partnership to more than 100 stores nationwide following a trial. Customers can now access up to more than 9,000 home improvement products through Deliveroo, with orders delivered in as little as 35 minutes.
The partnership with Gophr will allow Business Development Managers to arrange deliveries, either within two hours or for a pre-booked two-hour slot same-day, for TradePoint members from B&Q's standalone TradePoint store in Barking and 123 participating B&Q stores across the UK. The service is set to expand to all TradePoint stores later this year.
The launch builds on the introduction of Marketplace Click & Collect. Customers can now choose from an expanding range of collection and delivery options designed to suit planned projects, urgent repairs and last minute requirements.
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
AI and on demand delivery will be key focus areas at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards, which celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world, have now closed for entries. Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.

items.title: DoorDash snaps up Instacart as Morrisons ditches smart carts: this week's biggest retail technology stories
items.summary: It's Friday, the weekend is almost upon us, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful week for the retail tech space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from the past few days, including Co-op, Circana, Gap Inc., KFC UK & Ireland, Roblox, TFG London, CDS Superstores, 3D
items.body:
It's Friday, the weekend is almost upon us, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful week for the retail tech space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from the past few days, including Co-op, Circana, Gap Inc., KFC UK & Ireland, Roblox, TFG London, CDS Superstores, 3D Cloud, MillerKnoll, and Holland & Barrett.
1. Co-op and Circana extend data and insights tie up through new multi-year deal
Circana and Co-op have announced a new multi-year agreement, extending a partnership that launched in 2020.
Over the past few years, the former's HIVE portal has become a key part of Co-op’s data strategy, enabling the retailer and its suppliers to work from the same data and build a shared understanding of customer behaviour, category performance and market trends.
HIVE brings together EPoS transactions, shopper insights, loyalty metrics, purchasing behaviours and market performance to provide a single view of performance across the business.
The renewed agreement marks the next phase of HIVE’s development, with the aim of strengthening Co-op’s ability to unlock value from its data assets while helping suppliers make faster, more informed decisions.
Over the next five years, Circana and Co-op will expand the platform’s capabilities through the integration of new data assets and measurement solutions, including supply chain, quick commerce and wholesale insights.
Imran Rasul, Chief Commercial Officer, Co-op, says: “We are delighted to deepen and extend our relationship with Circana. The next evolution of HIVE will provide suppliers with broader, more connected insights across our business, enabling faster decision-making, stronger collaboration and greater opportunities for shared growth. Together, we're creating a platform that helps turn data into action and supports long-term success for both Co-op and its partners.”
2. Fashion retailer Gap Inc. starts scaling Bridgette, an AI tool for seasonal hiring, across stores and DCs
Gap Inc. has started to scale Bridgette, an AI enabled virtual career guide for seasonal hiring, across its stores and distribution centres.
Bridgette answers candidate questions at any hour, coordinates interviews and sends reminders. In a pilot, nearly 45,000 candidates engaged with it, and it has scheduled more than 7,000 interviews for store leaders.
In a LinkedIn post, Sven Gerjets, EVP and CTO at Gap Inc., said: "It works every day of the week, which is a better schedule than mine. What I care about most is what it does not do. Managers still run the interviews and make the hiring decisions. That is the point."
He added: "Our approach to AI is human centered and digitally enabled. For every step in a process, we ask what should be automated, what should be AI assisted, and what should stay with a person. Then we redesign the work around the outcome instead of speeding up the old process."
"Hiring is a good example, because the repetitive coordination was crowding out the conversations that build great teams. I keep coming back to a simple test. Does the technology give people their time back for the human work that matters most?"
3. DoorDash circles $17 billion Instacart acquisition as Caper Carts business is wound down
DoorDash is in advanced talks to acquire Instacart in a deal that could value the grocery technology specialist at around $17 billion, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal.
An agreement could be reached as soon as this week. Separately, Instacart said in a regulatory filing on Monday that it would wind down its Caper Cart smart cart business by the end of the second quarter of 2027, expecting pre-tax charges of $55 million to $80 million related to the move.
The plan is to reinvest any savings into strategic growth initiatives, which includes other in-store solutions like smart price tags and computer vision technology to help grocers track in-store inventory.
4. 'Not just a kids' platform anymore': KFC UK & Ireland launches on Roblox for first time
KFC UK & Ireland has launched on Roblox for the first time, with a Believer Rewards experience going live this week.
In a LinkedIn post, Nic Mitham, Director of Loyalty Growth, said: "I’m really proud of what the teams have built. Roblox isn’t just a kids’ platform anymore. A big and growing share of its players are adults and next-gen consumers, and we wanted KFC to show up for them with something worth having, while building a direct relationship through our own app."
He added: "We also wanted to do it properly. The experience is age gated to 18+ and fully HFSS compliant. Getting that right from the start was non-negotiable for us, and it shaped every decision about how the campaign was built."
Players start in the Believers Hub, then teleport into partner games across Roblox to unlock in-game boosts and rewards. Over the next eight weeks, KFC is releasing ten limited edition UGC items, including a bucket hat and a chicken suit. Customers can download the fast food giant's app, and switch on notifications in order to be in the know when each new item drops.
5. 3D Cloud and MillerKnoll furniture partnership brings product configurators to Knoll.com
3D Cloud and MillerKnoll have announced the deployment of 3D product configurators on Knoll.com.
MillerKnoll is using a centralised library to support digital experiences across its portfolio of furniture brands. The strategy aims to reduce duplication, maintain consistency, and speed the roll-out of interactive product configurators, including the latest launch on Knoll.com.
At the centre of the strategy is a shared foundation of scalable 3D product content and the full suite of 3D Cloud applications. Instead of treating every website, brand or customer experience as a separate 3D project, MillerKnoll says it can extend product content investments to each audience and point in the customer journey.
"We're preserving our design legacy in 3D, while looking toward the future of how customers and designers experience our brands," says Lorna Jean Marcuzzo, Senior Technology Manager, 3D Visualisation + Content at MillerKnoll. "An enterprise 3D content strategy enables us to launch new digital capabilities and experiences faster, maintain consistency across our portfolio, and maximise the value of every digital twin."
"The Knoll Womb Chair demonstrates this strategy in action. Its 3D product content and data, including materials, finishes, and configuration options, are centrally managed in one place that keeps customer experiences aligned and up to date across product offerings and digital touchpoints."
6. Holland & Barrett announces €17.5 million investment across digital and retail fulfilment in Ireland
UK health and wellness retailer, Holland and Barrett, has announced a €17.5 million investment across digital and retail fulfilment in Ireland over the next three years.
From 1st November, fulfilment of its Irish online orders will move from the UK to Ireland through an expanded three-year partnership with Kildare-based Road Truck Services (RTS), building on an eight-year relationship spanning import, customs, warehousing and distribution.
The move will see €8.2 million invested in a new digital fulfilment model, alongside €9.3 million relating to existing retail fulfilment operations with RTS, bringing the total investment to €17.5 million over the next three years.
Around €1.5 million of additional stock will be held locally, bringing Holland & Barrett’s total Irish stockholding to approximately €4.7 million. Around 328,000 orders and 1.8 million units are expected to flow through the Irish logistics network each year.
The expanded partnership is also expected to support around 20 additional RTS roles, alongside agency support during peak periods and a further 6-10 indirect roles, with recruitment focused on Kildare town and surrounding areas.
For customers, the move will mean greater choices on online orders from 1st November, with the existing 5kg weight limit lifted and additional products from 34 Irish brands available online. Next-day delivery is planned to launch from 1st December.
The investment comes as Holland & Barrett grows its presence in Ireland. Approximately 2.8 million customers shopped with the business over the past year, and it now operates 70 stores and employs 419 colleagues across the country.
7. CDS Superstores (The Range, Wilko, Homebase) and THG Fulfil agree multi-year extension of fulfilment tie up
THG Fulfil and CDS Superstores, trading as The Range, wilko and Homebase, have agreed a multi-year contract extension.
The deal builds on a partnership that began in 2024, in which THG Fulfil provides fulfilment and courier management services for the home, leisure and garden retailer.
The renewal supports CDS Superstores’ digital transformation as it looks to invest in technology to strengthen the online offer for The Range, wilko and Homebase. This includes Google Cloud AI technologies to improve search and product discovery on wilko.com, and Mirakl’s platform to support the growth of The Range’s online marketplace.
CDS Superstores is tapping THG Fulfil’s warehouse automation, with 95% of units sold passing through a form of automation during the fulfilment journey. This includes a fleet of Geekplus goods-to-person robots.
8. Morrisons bins Instacart AI powered Caper Carts trial amid DoorDash acquisition talks
In July, we reported that Morrisons had launched Instacart’s Caper Cart smart trolleys at a Preston supermarket, marking North American firm Instacart’s first retail partnership in the UK for its AI powered solution.
Three months later, however, the retailer is pulling the trial as DoorDash gets set to acquire Instacart in a deal that values the grocery technology specialist at around $17 billion. Separately, Instacart said in a regulatory filing on Monday that it would wind down its Caper Cart business by the end of the second quarter of 2027, expecting pre-tax charges of $55 million to $80 million related to the move.
The plan is to reinvest any savings into strategic growth initiatives, which includes other in-store solutions like smart price tags and computer vision technology to help grocers track in-store inventory.
"Our customers are at the heart of everything we do, and we're always looking for ways to make their weekly shop easier, more rewarding, and more enjoyable, to give them more reasons to shop at Morrisons," Gordon Macpherson, Productivity Director at Morrisons, said during the launch of the trial.
“Caper smart trolleys do exactly that, giving customers real-time visibility of their spending, instant access to their More Card savings, and a more seamless experience in the aisle. We're proud to be the first UK retailer to bring this technology to our customers, and we look forward to seeing how shoppers in Preston and across Lancashire respond to this innovative new trolley in this in-store trial.”
Morrisons did not respond to our request for comment regarding the pilot's abrupt end.
Responding to the news, retail analyst Steve Dresser said on LinkedIn: "Not one to mock innovation, it's vital. But this was always overplayed and seemed to be a chance for people to get their name in lights, rather than a meaningful trial to scale."
9. Revolut Pay one-click account-to-account payments go live on Just Eat app and online
Just Eat has announced a partnership with Revolut, meaning that the on demand delivery big hitter's customers can now select Revolut Pay for a one-click checkout experience within its app and online in the UK and Ireland.
To mark the launch, users can earn a 5x RevPoints boost on every Just Eat purchase between 28th October and 27th December. Following the promotional window, customers will retain a 2x points boost on every purchase, alongside the ability to instantly redeem RevPoints for cash discounts at the Just Eat app and web checkout.
Selecting this option means that customers will no longer need to manually input card details and can authorise restaurant and grocery orders using biometric authentication (Face ID or fingerprint recognition) through their Revolut account.
Michiel Verberg, Head of Global Strategic Partnerships at Just Eat, says: "We're always looking for ways to make ordering from Just Eat faster and more rewarding. Revolut Pay removes a step from checkout, and the RevPoints boost gives customers something back on every order. This is the start of two of Europe's leading technology companies building a better user experience together, which is good news for consumers."
10. Phase Eight owner TFG London contacts customers as personal data is accessed following cyber attack
The owner of Hobbs, Whistles and Phase Eight has contacted its customers following a cyber security incident earlier this month and urged them to be alert to unexpected emails, calls or text messages.
TFG London - the UK arm of retail conglomerate The Foschini Group - identified an incident on Sunday, 11th October affecting some IT systems and specifically impacting the Phase Eight, Hobbs, and Whistles fashion brands.
In an email sent to customers, dated 28th October, TFG London CEO Justin Hampshire said: "On identifying a cybersecurity incident affecting some of our IT systems, we acted immediately to secure our systems, brought in independent cybersecurity experts, and notified the relevant government authorities."
He added: "Unfortunately, our investigation has shown that some personal data has been accessed, and we wanted to contact you about this as soon as we could. We are contacting all of our customers as a precaution. This does not mean that your information was affected, and our investigation into exactly which information has been accessed is continuing."
The information affected could include contact and delivery details, order information, and in some cases limited payment information, such as the last four digits of a payment card. It doesn't include useable payment card details.
