items.title: Many self-checkouts in London convenience stores out of action due to technical faults, new research
items.summary: One in nine self-checkouts in London convenience stores are out of action at any given moment because of technical faults, according to new research released by Scalefusion.The research, covering 730 self-checkouts in 100 London stores run by four of the UK’s largest supermarket brands, found that o
items.body:
One in nine self-checkouts in London convenience stores are out of action at any given moment because of technical faults, according to new research released by Scalefusion.
The research, covering 730 self-checkouts in 100 London stores run by four of the UK’s largest supermarket brands, found that on average 11% of machines were unavailable to shoppers. In one instance, every self-checkout was running but none could take contactless card payments, a fault that lasted for several days in a row.
Scalefusion is warning that, with so many convenience stores competing for the same customers, a single faulty machine will create delays and queues that erode customer experience and drive business elsewhere.
The Virgin Media O2 Business Movers Index found that 38% of UK shoppers have left a store or avoided returning because of complicated or unreliable technology, rising to 51% among Gen Z. Self-checkouts top the list of frustrations, cited by 33%.
Sriram Kakarala, Chief Product Officer at Scalefusion, says: “Convenience stores depend on quick visits - if speed isn’t possible, they’re no longer convenient. And there’s an alternative on almost every urban street. Technology now plays a vital role in how consumers experience a brand. Every machine out of action means longer queues, frustrated staff and disappointed customers."
“As convenience estates grow, supermarket chains are managing tens of thousands of self-checkouts, so a small technical fault can quickly become an operational problem at scale. A machine that’s out of action ties up staff and sends customers to competitors. Retailers need to be able to fix faults remotely and rapidly to keep downtime to a minimum, or they risk losing both customers and revenue.”

His CV also includes stints at Michael Kors an
items.body:
Ethan Feinstein has joined Bath & Body Works as Director of Social Media Strategy.
He was previously at The Estée Lauder Companies where he spent five years, most recently serving as Senior Manager, Global Social & Influencer Marketing, Clinique. His CV also includes stints at Michael Kors and Coty.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: "Few brands have the kind of emotional connection Bath & Body Works does and I’m excited to bring fresh ideas to a brand this beloved."
"We're taking the brand in a bold new direction, and I'll be leading the charge across: Brand social: building always on channels that drive culture, community and conversion; Creators and talent: partnering with new and existing voices our community loves and trusts; Culturally relevant partnerships: showing up in the moments, conversations, and collabs that matter; IRL: bringing new and longtime fans into our evolving store experiences, because the magic of this brand still lives in walking through the door. Big ideas, an amazing team, and so much ahead!"
Scotland
Frasers Plus Braehead reports that Bath & Body Works is set to open its first standalone store in Scotland at the retail and leisure destination this winter. This is opening ahead of Christmas and will span more than 2,000 sq ft.
Rachel Scott, Head of Leasing at Global Mutual, comments: “Bath & Body Works’ decision to select Frasers Plus Braehead for its first standalone Scottish store is a significant endorsement of the destination’s regional reach and the momentum behind our evolving offer."
“Bath & Body Works will broaden our beauty offer across body care, home fragrance and gifting, while giving shoppers access to the full standalone store experience. Opening ahead of Christmas, it will introduce a strong new gifting proposition that complements the wider destination at a key trading moment.”
A spokesperson from Bath & Body Works, says: “Opening our first standalone Scottish store is an important milestone for Bath & Body Works, and Frasers Plus Braehead is the ideal location for this next step in our growth."
“The destination’s strong regional draw and impressive mix of leading retail brands made it a natural choice for our debut. We look forward to bringing the full Bath & Body Works experience to Braehead and building meaningful relationships with customers across Scotland.”

items.title: Bodycare builds micro-influencer network supporting high street comeback with PMC AI infrastructure
items.summary: Health and beauty retailer, Bodycare, says it is boosting its high street return with a community led social strategy, optimising content from its micro-influencer network with a custom built AI platform, designed and delivered in partnership with PMC.The retailer, which last year closed all its sto
items.body:
Health and beauty retailer, Bodycare, says it is boosting its high street return with a community led social strategy, optimising content from its micro-influencer network with a custom built AI platform, designed and delivered in partnership with PMC.
The retailer, which last year closed all its stores after collapsing into adminstration, is continuing its comeback, having opened five stores in Sheffield, Derby, Leicester, Bradford and Dudley. Blending commerce and experiences in-store, it now runs all store operations through its proprietary AI platform, AIMEE, which connects data across customers, inventory, trends, social content and store performance to continually improve decision-making.
Designed and built by PMC as the AI brain powering Bodycare’s store network, AIMEE underpins each store’s dedicated, free-to-use content production studios, which allow digital creators and micro-influencers to generate hyper-localised content that drives community engagement.
AIMEE onboards, briefs and collaborates with micro- and nano-influencers across Bodycare's creator community, while analysing regional social trends against store inventory to optimise content subsequently produced by creators and Bodycare's in-house production team.
“We're not just bringing Bodycare back to the high street; we're reimagining what a value led beauty store can be,” says Bodycare’s CMO, Tash Courtenay-Smith. “Our ambition is to create spaces that are as much about community, creativity and connection as they are about commerce, always giving shoppers that reason to pop in.”
“By putting creators at the heart of our store experiences - and using AI to connect social trends with what happens on the shop floor - we're creating a more responsive and relevant retail offering. Working with PMC, we've been able to turn that vision into reality, building a new generation of stores that are shaped by the communities they serve.”
Since its first store opening in July, Bodycare has onboarded 700 creators, with micro- and nano-influencer content now generating 7.5 million views. Insights from its digital creator network are then fed back into AIMEE, allowing the retailer to inform inventory allocation and forecasting based on live demand signals from social engagement.
Connecting the entire retail ecosystem, from social content creation through to in-store execution, AIMEE also informs the experiences delivered through PMC's Interact digital display solution. Supporting the wider in-store commerce experience, PMC has also deployed its Graphene Engage platform to power traditional, mobile and self-service checkout experiences.
“Bodycare is challenging the boundaries between physical retail, social commerce and AI to create a store model where content, community and commerce don’t just co-exist but become truly connected,” says Elliott Winskill, Technology & Solutions Director at PMC, who is also acting as Technical Lead at Bodycare.
“By building robust, composable foundations, we've enabled AIMEE to become the AI brain behind Bodycare's operations, supported by connected digital and transactional infrastructure that brings together social intelligence, customer engagement and store operations."
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
Bodycare and PMC have been shortlisted in two categories at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
Named as finalists in both the Bricks and Mortar and AI Innovation (UK) categories, the partnership has been recognised for bringing cutting-edge innovation and live AI use cases to physical retail environments.

items.body:
Very, the online retailer operated by The Very Group, is promising customers that what they pay on Black Friday offers will always be the cheapest, even if the same item is reduced further during its Black Friday event.
Running from 28th October to 4th December, this covers eligible offers across all shopping categories, including fashion, electricals, toys, home, beauty and sports. If Very reduces the price of an eligible product further during the event, customers can claim back the difference.
Robbie Feather, CEO at The Very Group, says: “Our Price Promise is all about giving customers greater confidence that they’re getting the best deal. For Black Friday, we’re going even further."
“One of the biggest decisions customers face during Black Friday is deciding whether to buy now or wait to see if prices fall even further. Our Price Promise removes that uncertainty. Customers can shop our deals as soon as they see them, safe in the knowledge that if we reduce the price of an eligible product later in the event, they won't miss out.”

items.title: Consumers show unmet appetite for AI shopping. Check out the retail technology week in numbers
items.summary: Do you like numbers? Do you like retail tech news? Then this is the article for you. Including easyShop, Klarna, M&S, Holland & Barrett, John Lewis, EE, SAI, DoorDash, Instacart, Carrefour Belgium, DPD UK, HyperFinity, Disney Store, KFC UK & Ireland, Debenhams Group, Walmart, Symbotic, a
items.body:
Do you like numbers? Do you like retail tech news? Then this is the article for you. Including easyShop, Klarna, M&S, Holland & Barrett, John Lewis, EE, SAI, DoorDash, Instacart, Carrefour Belgium, DPD UK, HyperFinity, Disney Store, KFC UK & Ireland, Debenhams Group, Walmart, Symbotic, and Ocado Group.
25 and $6 million...Symbotic and Walmart have announced an expanded tie up to bring automation capabilities to 25 US regional distribution centres, while supporting additional opportunities across the retail giant's global supply chain network.
The agreement includes an initial commitment of approximately $6 billion in spend, covering work over several years.
“Our partnership with Walmart started with a single product over a decade ago, and now we offer a full end-to-end solution to help power Walmart’s growth across its supply chain for years to come,” says Rick Cohen, Chairman and CEO at Symbotic. “This expanded agreement reflects the strength of that collaboration - a partnership defined by trust and shared ambition.”
1...KFC UK & Ireland has launched on Roblox for the first time, with a Believer Rewards experience going live this week.
In a LinkedIn post, Nic Mitham, Director of Loyalty Growth, said: "I’m really proud of what the teams have built. Roblox isn’t just a kids’ platform anymore. A big and growing share of its players are adults and next-gen consumers, and we wanted KFC to show up for them with something worth having, while building a direct relationship through our own app."
He added: "We also wanted to do it properly. The experience is age gated to 18+ and fully HFSS compliant. Getting that right from the start was non-negotiable for us, and it shaped every decision about how the campaign was built."
Players start in the Believers Hub, then teleport into partner games across Roblox to unlock in-game boosts and rewards. Over the next eight weeks, KFC is releasing ten limited edition UGC items, including a bucket hat and a chicken suit. Customers can download the fast food giant's app, and switch on notifications in order to be in the know when each new item drops.
19...easyShop.com, a new online marketplace from the easy family of brands, has added buy now pay later option, Klarna, to checkout across 19 European markets.
Customers shopping on easyShop can now choose Klarna's Pay in Full, Pay in 3 or Pay in 30 options, allowing them to pay upfront, split a purchase into three interest free payments, or pay a month later.
The partnership follows easyShop's launch earlier this month and comes as the venture prepares for its first peak trading period.
Cas Paton, Founder and CEO at OnCommerce, the platform powering easyShop, says: "Black Friday is no longer just about finding the best deal. Shoppers also want flexibility in how they pay. By bringing Klarna to easyShop, we're giving customers the freedom to shop in a way that suits them, while helping our sellers capitalise on one of the biggest retail moments of the year."
"The easy family of brands has always been about making things simpler and more accessible. Adding Klarna is another way we’re delivering on that, giving shoppers more choice alongside great products and competitive prices."
72...Metricool, a social media management platform, has released a report analysing how 72 e-commerce brands, including BÉIS, Bombas, Ruggable and YETI, use Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and YouTube to showcase products, engage consumers and support the path to purchase.
The company analysed 3,234 posts published by 72 US e-commerce brands across Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and YouTube between 1st-31st August.
The sample covered seven categories: fashion and apparel, home decor and furniture, consumer tech and gadgets, beauty and personal care, pet products, outdoor and fitness gear, and food and beverage/CPG.
The findings point to a disconnect between the content brands publish and how they facilitate purchases, with overtly promotional posts often performing the weakest.
70...Marks & Spencer has unveiled the first wave of jobs available at its new automated fashion distribution centre in Lichfield, set to open next year.
Over 70 vacancies are now available on the M&S Careers website, including management, operational and specialist roles. The 437,000 sq ft logistics warehouse is expected to employ 600 people in total when fully operational.
It will add additional capacity to M&S’ existing 24/7 distribution network, enabling it to more quickly process and move orders from suppliers to distribution centres and then onto stores or direct to customers. The retailer is aiming to double online fashion, home and beauty sales, with supply chain transformation a key part of its reshaping for growth strategy.
63,000...UK parcel delivery company DPD has opened a new 63,000 sq ft distribution centre (DC) at Forrest Park, near Darlington, County Durham.
Part of a multimillion-pound investment announcement in March last year, the DC will increase DPD’s capacity in the North East of England.
The new hub - located adjacent to Junction 59 of the A1(M) - has the potential to create up to 250 additional roles as DPD expands its operations in the region. The automated sortation facility will be capable of processing up to 50,000 parcels a day. It has also been developed to BREEAM Excellent standards.
Justin Pegg, DPD UK CEO, comments: “I’m delighted to see our brand new Darlington DC open on schedule as we head towards our busiest time of the year. We are planning for a record Black Friday and Christmas peak period this year and our network of over 80 distribution centres is absolutely key to the campaign."
"This is an ongoing programme and we have consistently invested in building brand new DCs for the last 15 years. As a result, the majority of our network is made up of purpose-built facilities with the automation and the capacity we need to run a premium national seven day a week, next day delivery service, helping to ensure we always meet the demand for our services and exceed our customers’ expectations.”
15...Polytag has expanded its Ecotrace Programme into Scotland, installing its UV tag detection technology at Wyllie Recycling’s material recovery facility (MRF) in Perth.
Polytag’s tech detects invisible UV tags activated on packaging as it passes through enabled recycling facilities, capturing barcode level data about which tagged packaging is detected, and where and when. Depending on the information encoded, the tags can also provide additional details about packaging, including plastic melt flow temperature, the packaging converter and food-grade status.
These insights can help businesses assess packaging performance, inform packaging design and build a clearer evidence base for recycling outcomes as the UK’s Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) system evolves.
The installation marks Polytag’s 15th UV detection unit. Wyllie Recycling operates a 4.5-acre MRF in Perth, processing twin-stream kerbside recycling for multiple Scottish local authorities. Brands like Ocado Retail and Waitrose are using Polytag’s network of detection units to gather data on their packaging.
€17.5 million...UK health and wellness retailer, Holland and Barrett, has announced a €17.5 million investment across digital and retail fulfilment in Ireland over the next three years.
From 1st November, fulfilment of its Irish online orders will move from the UK to Ireland through an expanded three-year partnership with Kildare-based Road Truck Services (RTS), building on an eight-year relationship spanning import, customs, warehousing and distribution.
The move will see €8.2 million invested in a new digital fulfilment model, alongside €9.3 million relating to existing retail fulfilment operations with RTS, bringing the total investment to €17.5 million over the next three years.
Around €1.5 million of additional stock will be held locally, bringing Holland & Barrett’s total Irish stockholding to approximately €4.7 million. Around 328,000 orders and 1.8 million units are expected to flow through the Irish logistics network each year.
The expanded partnership is also expected to support around 20 additional RTS roles, alongside agency support during peak periods and a further 6-10 indirect roles, with recruitment focused on Kildare town and surrounding areas.
For customers, the move will mean greater choices on online orders from 1st November, with the existing 5kg weight limit lifted and additional products from 34 Irish brands available online. Next-day delivery is planned to launch from 1st December.
The investment comes as Holland & Barrett grows its presence in Ireland. Approximately 2.8 million customers shopped with the business over the past year, and it now operates 70 stores and employs 419 colleagues across the country.
25...Happy birthday to JohnLewis.com! This week marked 25-years since John Lewis and Partners launched its online service back in 2001.
The first product sold was beech salt and pepper mill. In a LinkedIn post, the retailer said: "Fast forward to 2026 and it's fair to say we couldn't imagine a time without it. If you haven't already, download the John Lewis app and start unlocking My John Lewis member benefits today."
Simon Fulford, Head of Change Delivery and Technology, added: "I’m proud to be a small part of this 25 year journey, in an age where technology is changing faster than ever before."
"A big thank you to the hundreds, if not thousands, of people over that period that have contributed over that time. Here’s to the next 25 years and all the exciting changes we have to come!"
29% of AI shoppers say AI chat or search tools had the biggest influence on their most recent purchase - three times the share citing traditional search engines (9%), and more than retailers’ platforms and AI assistants combined (21%), according to new McKinsey & Company research drawing on a survey of approximately 21,000 consumers in 11 markets.
The shift is moving beyond discovery to influence and transactions. In the US, the share of AI users completing a purchase through AI has surged 70% since December 2025, from 10% to 17%.
Kelsey Robinson, Senior Partner, McKinsey & Company, says: "Consumers are showing unmet appetite and preference for AI shopping. Nearly a third of AI shoppers said AI chat or search tools were the biggest influence on their recent purchase. The winners this holiday season will be those that have stood up an agentic capability and are treating this as an always-on experimentation muscle."
44%...With Ofcom due to set out its enforcement plan for next year’s social media ban in the coming days, research from EE reveals that two in five 11 to 15-year-olds are already planning to dodge the restrictions by downloading apps that fall outside the new rules.
A survey of 1,000 UK parents of secondary school children, 1,000 young people aged 11 to 17, and 100 secondary school teachers found that 44% of secondary school pupils are talking about possible workarounds with their friends, including scoping out alternative platforms that may not be covered by the ban, and 95% of teachers expect at least some to succeed.
Young people who switch to apps outside the ban, such as new messaging services, gaming sites or lesser known social platforms, will not be covered by its protections. This could leave them exposed to the very risks the restrictions were designed to prevent, from bullying and harmful content to addictive algorithmic feeds.
Yet just 44% of parents know the ban arrives in March, raising the risk that conversations about staying safe online happen too late, after children have already started looking for workarounds and navigating alternative spaces.
24,000...DPD UK has announced a programme delivering 24,000 mentoring sessions in its first year to 16 to 25 year olds across the UK.
Up to 2,000 DPD UK colleagues will participate in the initiative, volunteering at least 30 minutes each per month for 12 months to virtually support young people with careers advice on everything from how to improve a CV, to preparing for an interview, and building confidence to face a difficult job market. Thousands of young people are set to be involved, and they can come back for a second or third session.
This is an attempt to address the crisis of 981,000 young people aged 16 to 24 (13.0%) classified as NEET (not in education, employment or training) in the UK, according to the latest ONS figures, with the youth unemployment rate for 16 to 24-year-olds standing at 15.8%.
The programme was developed and will be facilitated by mentorhero, a new global mentoring platform co-founded by Jackson Parsons who hosts career show 'My Duvet Flip', also aimed at supporting young people with careers advice content, with more than one million subscribers on YouTube.
61% and 28%...Younger shoppers are the most likely to abandon a retailer over its loyalty scheme, despite feeling more loyal to retailers than they did three years ago, according to new research from HyperFinity, Bloomreach, and Eagle Eye.
The research, which surveyed 2,000 Brits who belong to loyalty programmes, found that 61% of under-35s feel more loyal to retailers than they did three years ago, yet 28% have stopped shopping with a retailer because of its loyalty programme. This is compared with just 10% of over-65s.
Thomas Hill, Co-founder at HyperFinity, says: “Younger shoppers may feel more loyal to retailers, but that loyalty cannot be taken for granted. A scheme that offers generic rewards or fails to deliver on its promises can quickly undermine that relationship. There is no one-size-fits-all approach to loyalty - retailers need to understand what individual customers value and make sure the benefits they offer are relevant, worthwhile and deliverable.”
While Halloween is now one of the biggest sales events of the UK retail calendar, heightened footfall in-store alongside ongoing economic pressures on household finances mean the spooky season has become a growing target for theft.
Data from SAI's One Platform, which analyses insight from more than 1,000 UK retail locations and inputs from over 30,000 cameras every day, showed that in 2025 Halloween (Friday, 31st Oct) shoplifting rose by +67% on the daily average.
This year, with Halloween falling on a Saturday - consistently one of the highest risk days of the week for retail crime - shoplifting is forecast to rise 150% year-on-year.
Partial payment is expected to make up the majority of shoplifting attempts (58%). This is followed by grab and go theft (33%) and item switching, where a shopper deliberately selects a lower priced product at self-checkout in place of a higher value item (8%).
$17 billion...DoorDash is in advanced talks to acquire Instacart in a deal that could value the grocery technology specialist at around $17 billion, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal.
An agreement could be reached as soon as this week. Separately, Instacart said in a regulatory filing on Monday that it would wind down its Caper Cart smart cart business by the end of the second quarter of 2027, expecting pre-tax charges of $55 million to $80 million related to the move.
The plan is to reinvest any savings into strategic growth initiatives, which includes other in-store solutions like smart price tags and computer vision technology to help grocers track in-store inventory.
1...Disney Store has announced the opening of its first UK Outlet store at McArthurGlen Designer Outlet Cheshire Oaks this autumn. This will offer a mix of new and seasonal full-price products alongside discounted merchandise, multibuy promotions and special offers.
Outlet stores have been a part of Disney Store’s international retail business for several years.
Located in Unit 170 at Cheshire Oaks, and spanning 1,300 sq ft, the store will offer a range of official merchandise, including products inspired by Disney, Pixar, MARVEL and Star Wars. The assortment will include toys, apparel, accessories, stationery, plush, collectibles and dress-up collections. Selected products will offer savings of up to 40%, with multibuy deals and other promotions also available.
The location will join Disney Store’s wider UK and Ireland retail network, alongside its standalone stores on Oxford Street in London and Grafton Street in Dublin, as well as locations inside Selfridges London, Selfridges Birmingham and Selfridges Manchester Trafford.
Patrick Sager, VP, Global Disney Store Retail & Marketing, says: “Outlet stores have been a successful part of our retail business around the world for several years. As the UK retail landscape and customer shopping habits continue to evolve, we’re excited to open our first UK Outlet store at Cheshire Oaks."
“The pop up will allow us to reach more guests and offer a wider range of price points, helping more guests bring home a little Disney wonder. By bringing together new and seasonal products, discounted merchandise and special offers, the store will provide families and fans with another way to shop official Disney merchandise in person, complementing our existing retail portfolio and online offering.”
1,200...Debenhams Group, home to Debenhams, PrettyLittleThing, boohoo, MAN and Karen Millen, has announced plans to move its fulfilment operations back to Burnley, through a new global distribution partnership with GXO Logistics. The move is expected to create over 1,200 jobs.
Dan Finley, CEO at Debenhams Group, says: “We’re delighted to be returning to Burnley. Burnley has played an important role in the group’s history, as the primary distribution location for over a decade. We’re excited to be combining our years of experience operating in the town with GXO’s fulfilment expertise, to support the next phase of the group’s growth."
In September, the group announced the £90 million sale of its Sheffield distribution centre to Primark. Debenhams Group expects to continue operating from Sheffield until early 2027, ahead of the transfer to Burnley. GXO will run the Burnley facility under a new agreement to oversee Debenhams Group’s global third-party distribution.
Russell Atkinson, Managing Director of Fashion and Apparel, GXO UK&I, says: “We’re excited to begin this new partnership with Debenhams, bringing GXO’s retail logistics expertise and global network to support its continued growth.”
12...Carrefour Belgium reports that it has hit the milestone of 12 autonomous BuyBye stores.
A Carrefour Belgium spokesperson said: "Making our customers' lives easier is also being present where a traditional store cannot be. With the opening of two new modules in the heart of the Charleroi hospital and soon three units in Lyon in partnership with Carrefour France, our AI driven autonomous concept is a new strategic milestone."
They added: "Why choose a hospital environment? To meet the very specific needs of caregivers and visitors, with fresh, balanced and affordable meal solutions, 24/7. At the reception desk of the hospital: a module accessible to patients, employees and visitors."
"Close to the entrance to the operating theatre: a solution especially for the 200 to 300 professionals who are constantly working there, so that they can quickly eat something during their shifts. This strengthens our network, which is already present in hospitals, army bases, stations, airports, campuses and corporate offices."
2...Ocado Group and AEON have announced the official go live of their second customer fulfilment centre (CFC) in Japan. The facility in Hachioji City, Tokyo was unveiled by AEON executives at a ceremony at the site.
This will provide additional capacity to enable the growth of AEON’s Green Beans online grocery delivery brand across the Tokyo region, as well as driving logistical efficiency and shorter delivery distances across its network. Hachioji is the second Ocado CFC to use its Auto-Freezer system following the recent launch of Lotte's CFC in Busan, South Korea.
This uses a specialised version of Ocado’s fulfilment bot to process frozen orders 2.7 times faster than AEON’s first CFC in Chiba, and increases freezer inventory capacity by 150% while reducing the required storage footprint by 50%. The Auto-Freezer will also reduce the time spent by staff in freezer conditions to below 5% of their working hours.
The four-storey CFC has a gross floor area of approximately 40,000 m², and is equipped with a full suite of Ocado’s Re:Imagined technologies, including On-Grid Robotic Pick. The site will also offer a Pickup service, allowing customers to collect orders directly from the site in as little as three hours.

items.title: Retail technology innovation of the week: Gap Inc. starts to scale AI powered Bridgette hiring tool
items.summary: Retail Technology Innovation of the Week is a series brought to you by RTIH, highlighting stand out deployments, launches, and initiatives by retailers and tech suppliers.Every week, we showcase forward thinking tech plays that have impressed our Editor and the Retail Technology Innovations Report j
items.body:
Retail Technology Innovation of the Week is a series brought to you by RTIH, highlighting stand out deployments, launches, and initiatives by retailers and tech suppliers.
Every week, we showcase forward thinking tech plays that have impressed our Editor and the Retail Technology Innovations Report judging panel, building up to the publication of the 2026 report later this year.
And this week we’re focusing on Gap Inc. which has started to scale Bridgette, an AI enabled virtual career guide for seasonal hiring, across its stores and distribution centres.
Bridgette answers candidate questions at any hour, coordinates interviews and sends reminders. In a pilot, nearly 45,000 candidates engaged with it, and it has scheduled more than 7,000 interviews for store leaders.
In a LinkedIn post, Sven Gerjets, EVP and CTO at Gap Inc., said: "It works every day of the week, which is a better schedule than mine. What I care about most is what it does not do. Managers still run the interviews and make the hiring decisions. That is the point."
He added: "Our approach to AI is human centred and digitally enabled. For every step in a process, we ask what should be automated, what should be AI assisted, and what should stay with a person. Then we redesign the work around the outcome instead of speeding up the old process."
"Hiring is a good example, because the repetitive coordination was crowding out the conversations that build great teams. I keep coming back to a simple test. Does the technology give people their time back for the human work that matters most?"
And honourable mentions this week to...
KFC UK & Ireland
KFC UK & Ireland has launched on Roblox for the first time, with a Believer Rewards experience going live this week.
In a LinkedIn post, Nic Mitham, Director of Loyalty Growth, said: "I’m really proud of what the teams have built. Roblox isn’t just a kids’ platform anymore. A big and growing share of its players are adults and next-gen consumers, and we wanted KFC to show up for them with something worth having, while building a direct relationship through our own app."
He added: "We also wanted to do it properly. The experience is age gated to 18+ and fully HFSS compliant. Getting that right from the start was non-negotiable for us, and it shaped every decision about how the campaign was built."
Players start in the Believers Hub, then teleport into partner games across Roblox to unlock in-game boosts and rewards. Over the next eight weeks, KFC is releasing ten limited edition UGC items, including a bucket hat and a chicken suit. Customers can download the fast food giant's app, and switch on notifications in order to be in the know when each new item drops.
Auchan Retail Romania
Auchan Retail Romania has launched a smart cart pilot powered by shopreme snap cart software on Hanshow tablets. Twenty four tablets are now available at one Auchan store, providing an additional self-checkout option alongside shopreme's mobile Scan & Pay solution, which has been available at the retailer since 2022.
As the pilot store also operates shopreme Scan & Pay, no separate integration was required for the new touchpoint. The smart carts deployment builds on the retailer’s existing PoS and loyalty integrations, employee processes, and backend environment.
Shoppers scan their loyalty card to unlock a tablet at a charging station. They then scan products as they shop, follow their live basket on the smart cart screen, and get personalised offers and loyalty benefits. At the end of the journey, the digital basket is transferred to the self-checkout kiosk, where the shopper completes payment.
Age verification, spot checks, and identification of customers who need assistance can be handled through an app that is already in use and also established workflows.

items.title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes
items.summary: A new generation is embracing eye-catching patching and visible mends.
items.body:
From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes
- Published
If Alice Brown is browsing in second-hand shops and finds a jumper with a hole, that won't stop her buying it.
"I see it as challenge," says the 27-year-old forest ranger from Lincolnshire.
She is a champion of the growing fashion for eye-catching repairs.
Over the last year she has developed her own unique style, needle-felting cute animals and insects to cover moth holes, stains and other imperfections, winning her a huge following online.
"The natural place for decoration is in the centre at the front. If the hole is under the arm or on the shoulder, it forces you to think about the design," she says.
Often dubbed "visible mending" the trend is spreading from hobby crafters and community workshops, even drawing in fast-fashion brands and reaching the designer catwalks this year.
At one Saturday morning workshop in Brighton, Jayne Eagle shows her students how to attach a patch of fabric behind a tear so the cat-face design peeps through.
Then she instructs them in stitching techniques inspired by the traditional Japanese methods Boro and Sashiko. Instead of matching the thread colour to the garment, they make the mend highly decorative using geometric patterns in large white stitching.
She also offers classes in darning using contrasting vibrant colours that celebrate, rather than disguise, the repair.
One student, Nicola, has already used her newfound skills to stitch over sunscreen marks on a T-shirt "making a feature of it" and is now delighted that people "stop seeing the stains and just see the decoration".
Another student, Lisa, says her mother's generation would never have wanted the mends to show. "Now part of it is being proud of what you've done," she says.
Lisa bought a second-hand jacket online, but snipped the fabric with the scissors when she was opening the package. She managed to patch it in a way that "looks intentional".
"I was actually pointing it out to people," she laughs.
In the past mending was primarily about saving money, by wearing clothes for longer, rather than buying new. But visible mending is about celebrating that choice.
The trend took off about six years ago, Jayne says, and has boomed since.
An era of "throwaway" fast fashion from the 1980s onwards undermined the tradition of looking after and mending your clothes and people lost the skills, she says.
The revival of interest feels to her like a backlash against overproduction in the fashion industry and the damage it causes: the pollution, carbon emissions, water use, and poor labour conditions.
So perhaps it is surprising just how popular mended style is proving among retailers, with brands from Ralph Lauren to ultra-fast-fashion firm Shein currently selling stitched and patched garments, albeit in both of those cases brand new off the peg.
Other High Street chains are adopting a more authentic approach, offering in-house repairs and workshops.
"We want to give customers practical ways to extend the life of the clothes they already love, rather than simply replacing them," says Uniqlo's head of sustainability, Maria Ledous.
Primark, often seen as a fast-fashion retailer due to its lower prices, has also joined the trend.
"We don't think that affordability and durability should be opposites," says Vicki Swain, the brand's longevity lead.
Outdoor brand Finisterre says around a fifth of the mends it provides for customers are designed to be eye-catching, while premium artisan clothing store Toast says around a third of customers go for that option.
Part of the "magic" is that customers can bring in a garment and "choose what they'd like it to become next", says Toast chief executive Suzie de Rohan Willner.
Toast's repair services are free, but off-the-peg "renewed" pieces fetch higher prices than the originals to reflect their unique character.
Levi's, which boasts probably the longest tradition of being fixed up by its fans using anything from rhinestones to fringed cuffs, is rolling out a workshop programme this year.
The firm says its research shows younger customers in particular want to repair more but don't know how.
For now, Levi's' workshops focus on traditional mending skills, such as sewing on a button and hemming, rather than visible mends, and at a recent launch event in London, that seemed to be what its Gen Z participants were looking for.
"I'm from East London. If you have holes in your clothes people are like 'Ha ha! You're poor!'," says 16-year-old school student Bianca.
Theo, 19, says he'd rather learn how to mend without it showing.
"I would want [the jeans] to look how I originally bought them," he says.
He has a side hustle selling clothes at car boot sales and thinks traditional repair skills would make it more lucrative.
His friend Nicholas, also 19, says most people want to look "fresh".
"No-one wants to look like they came out of a dumpster," he says.
Still, Paul Dillinger, Levi's head of global design innovation, thinks more creative repairs will win them over as they pick up more skills.
"No-one has time for that perfect 'straight from the shop' thing. That's not cool.
"People crave agency," he says. "Mending is a demonstration of humanity: it's not a mustard stain, it's a memory of a great day in the ballpark."

items.title: Amazon gives Wall Street mixed financial picture in earnings report
items.summary: E-commerce company posts high cloud computing sales but gives a cautious sales forecast for the fourth quarter Amazon offered a mixed picture of its financial health on Thursday in its quarterly earnings report. The e-commerce company gave a cautious sales forecast for the current fourth quarter, which encompasses the critical holiday shopping period, after delivering fiscal third-quarter results that came in below Wall Street analysts’ expectations. Continue reading...
items.body:
Amazon offered a mixed picture of its financial health on Thursday in its quarterly earnings report.
The e-commerce company gave a cautious sales forecast for the current fourth quarter, which encompasses the critical holiday shopping period, after delivering fiscal third-quarter results that came in below Wall Street analysts’ expectations.
The Seattle-based company posted strong growth, however, in its prominent cloud computing unit. Sales in its cloud computing unit, called AWS, rose 39.3% during the latest quarter ended 30 September, higher than the 37% clip in the previous quarter. It marked the fastest growth rate in nearly five years, the company said.
Still, shares were down more than 6% in after-market trading when the results were released as investors focused on the core business.
The tech company said earlier this month that it would hire 300,000 US seasonal workers for the shopping period, up from 250,000 last year.
Investors also have been closely watching Amazon’s quarterly earnings to see if the company’s big spending on artificial intelligence is starting to pay off.
Andy Jassy, the company’s CEO and president, disclosed to investors in July that Amazon now expects capital spending, mostly on artificial intelligence, to total $220bn for this fiscal year. That number includes outlays on robots, semiconductors and satellites. That’s up from the $200bn investment plan that was announced in February and well above the $128bn in capital spending for all of last year. Jassy had cited the higher cost of memory chips as the main reason for the increase.
Jassy told investors this past summer that even at the $220bn level, Amazon will not have enough capacity to meet all of its customers’ demands this year.
The latest earnings report from Alphabet late Wednesday raised alarm bells when it reported weaker growth for the summer than analysts expected. The company behind Google and YouTube also said it burned through more cash during the latest quarter, according to a measure called free cashflow, after its purchases of property and equipment topped $51bn. Its stock plummeted on Thursday, erasing half a trillion dollars in from the company’s total value.
Such worries are weighing on the entire AI industry following a big push to build datacenters and fill them with AI chips.
Amazon reported net income of $20.69bn, or $1.89 per share, in the three-month period. That compares with $21.19bn, or $1.95 per share, in the year-ago period.
Sales rose to $201.94bn, compared with the same year-ago period’s $180.17bn.
Analysts were expecting $1.97 per share on sales of $202.2bn, according to FactSet.
For the fourth quarter, Amazon said it expected net sales to be between $240bn and $247bn, which translates to a 12% to 16% increase compared with the year-ago period. Analysts were expecting $244.16bn.

items.title: Burnham 'ready to support' Poundland staff as retailer faces collapse
items.summary: Poundland's bosses are filing a notice of intention to appoint administrators to the business.
items.body:
Burnham 'ready to support' Poundland staff as retailer faces collapse
- Published
Andy Burnham has said the government is "ready to support" Poundland staff as the retailer teeters on the brink of collapse.
The prime minister called for answers over why an offer to buy the business from its current owners, which would have protected jobs, was rejected.
"This is a deeply worrying time for Poundland staff and their families," Burnham told the BBC.
The discount chain is teetering on the edge after its US-based owners Gordon Brothers cut off a vital funding supply and rejected a takeover offer from Irish firm Martin Property Group (MPG).
Burnham said: "We want to see jobs protected. If there was a potential owner to avoid this that hasn't been accepted, then the Business Secretary and I want to know why that is the case.
"We stand ready to support the workforce however we can."
The retailer's bosses have filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, giving the business 10 days to find a rescue deal.
The move comes after managing director Barry Williams told its 12,000 staff the chain's US owner had cut off a vital supply of funding despite Poundland's strong sales.
It is understood Gordon Brothers wants to break it up, with rivals Poundstretcher, B&M and Lidl interested in potentially buying up its stores.
Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds earlier said he was "very much concerned" by the uncertainty clouding Poundland's future.
Gordon Brothers bought Poundland, which had been struggling, from the Polish retail group Pepco last year for a nominal Â£1. A little over a year later, it put the business up for sale.
Despite an offer on the table for the business, Poundland's managers and owners have not been able to agree on a buyer, which has left it on the brink of collapse.
It could still be purchased out of administration in a so-called pre-pack deal, but the most likely option is for it to be broken up and for Poundland's stores to be sold off.
Poundland was founded in 1990 with a store in Burton-upon-Trent, and has around 20 million customers per year.
It has across its 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, where it trades as Dealz.
It sells low-cost everyday products, general merchandise and fashion on local high streets.
- The curious case of why Poundland is struggling during a cost-of-living crisis 
  - Published21 November 2025
- Poundland in rescue talks as owners seek buyer 
  - Published13 October
A Gordon Brothers insider said breaking the firm up would allow creditors to recover more money, and that this process would ultimately offer the best outcome for staff. The US investment firm's position is that current employees may be able to get employment with new store owners.
If this type of insolvency happens, it would let interested parties firm up offers.
These include Poundstretcher owner, Fortress, which according to one insider is interested in taking on between 200 and 250 stores.
Another large retailer is understood to be interested in buying up more than 100 other sites.
More than half a dozen retailers, include Iceland, Lidl, and B&M, have expressed interest in Poundland's store estate.
Bally Auluk, a national officer at the Usdaw shopworkers union, said this week had been "incredibly distressing" for Poundland staff.
He claimed staff were having to "watch from the sidelines as a multi-billion pound company jeopardises their livelihoods as it tries to extract Â£30m from a business it bought for Â£1".
He said Williams had "reluctantly" kicked off the administration process, to give the business time to find a rescue deal, adding that Usdaw was urging Gordon Brothers to reconsider.
The uncertainty surrounding Poundland's future has left some staff fearful about the future of their jobs.
Staff at Poundland's customer support centre in Walsall, some dressed as the Poundland "Pound Hound" mascot, held a protest on Thursday.
One employee said they were trying to "save our jobs".
Situation 'wholly avoidable'
There is also a split between the owners and the management running Poundland, who described the situation as "unexpected, unwanted and wholly avoidable".
"As you all know, our sales are strong and our recovery is taking root. This business simply does not deserve to go into any kind of administration," the chain's managing director Williams said in a message to staff this week.
He revealed that Gordon Brothers had limited Poundland's access to funds which help it run its day-to-day business.
"I'm disappointed to have to tell you that Gordon Brothers have given instructions that restricts our access to funds that we would, in normal circumstances expect to access fully under our existing loan agreement," he added.
In the memo, seen by the BBC, Williams said the offer from Martin Property Group was a "fully funded, ready to go bid that would have kept the business intact and able to continue the remarkable progress we've made".
Three independent directors who were appointed earlier this month to help oversee a sale resigned with immediate effect after disagreeing with Gordon Brothers' decision not to accept MPG's solvent offer.
Gordon Brothers has lined up AlixPartners as administrators.

Do you work for Poundland? Share your experience.

items.title: Andy Burnham pushes for answers as Poundland edges towards collapse - what next for retailer?
items.summary: Andy Burnham has now said he is willing to demand answers over the retailer's owners' handling of a sales process. The Prime Minister said it was a 'deeply worrying time' for staff and their families.
items.body:
Andy Burnham pushes for answers as Poundland edges towards collapse - what next for retailer?
Poundland could disappear from the High Street within days as Andy Burnham asks questions over how its owners handled a sales process.
Thousands of nervous staff are waiting to hear what will happen to the discount retailer after it filed a notice to appoint administrators with the High Court today.
This will give the business, bought by US investment firm Gordon Brothers for less than £1 last year, some breathing room – ten days – to find a rescue deal. AlixPartners is poised to take over a potential insolvency process.
But the Poundland brand and its 600 shops will not be sold as a whole, leading to a carve-up of the 36-year old retailer, meaning jobs are at risk at any shops that are not bought.
And on Thursday night, the Prime Minister said he is ready to demand answers from owners amid a 'deeply worrying time' for staff and their families.
Burnham told The Telegraph: 'We want to see jobs protected. If there was a potential owner to avoid this that hasn’t been accepted, then the Business Secretary and I want to know why that is the case.'
Battle for survival: The fate of Poundland's near 12,000 staff hangs in the balance.
It would mark the biggest high street collapse since Debenhams closed its doors in 2021 with the loss of 12,000 jobs.
Job losses could hit 600 shops and a distribution centre in Makerfield, Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s constituency, which employs around 270 people.
Business secretary Jonathan Reynolds also said he was ‘very much concerned’ and would push for answers as workers and bosses seethe over its failure to find a buyer.
He told The Telegraph: ‘If it is true that it was not necessary to put the business into administration then the present owners will have to account for that.’
Why has Poundland struggled?
Chains like Poundland are battling shoppers with constrained budgets while costs, such as employing people, have increased – following Government moves to hike wages and employer National Insurance contributions. Savvier shoppers are looking for cheaper online alternatives, including Amazon, Temu and TikTok Shop.
Former owners, the Warsaw-listed Pepco Group, made some wrong moves that did not go down well with its customers, including putting Pepco clothing in its shops.
Its most recent woes stem back to last year, when it narrowly avoided collapsing into administration. The chain was sold in June 2025 to US firm Gordon Brothers for a nominal €1 amid 'challenging trading conditions'.
By November 2025, around 100 Poundland shops had been shut or earmarked for closure. Two months later, as part of its radical turnaround plan, Poundland had shut 149 stores with 2,200 job losses.
But this year, Poundland bosses insisted it was turning a corner, pointing to like-for-like sales growth of 3.3 per cent in the three months to September 26.
Poundland's managing director Barry Williams said earlier this month: 'Our recovery plan is working, thanks to our investment in simple low pricing and new ranges, powered by our new in-house teams.'
Why is there a dispute between Poundland’s owners and its bosses?
Both shop workers’ union Usdaw and Poundland’s management have accused Gordon Brothers of mishandling a sales process, which it kicked off at the beginning of September.
The union met with the minister for the future of work, Kate Dearden, on Wednesday, amid warnings of what would be the biggest High Street collapse in years.
Three directors, appointed less than a fortnight ago, this week walked out following a dramatic dispute with owners Gordon Brothers.
Hours later the retailer’s management hit out at the owners, calling the process ‘unexpected, unwanted and avoidable’.
Government adviser David Bickerton is set to ask ‘fairly basic questions of senior people around Poundland’ in order to ‘establish what the situation is,’ on behalf of the business secretary, the Financial Times reported.
What does a notice to appoint administrators mean?
‘Filing a notice of intention isn’t administration itself,’ explains Julie Palmer, managing partner at real estate advisory group BTG.
Instead, it effectively keeps the wolves from the door for up to ten business days of protection and helps the firm preserve cash.
She added: ‘If an appointment follows, the administrators take control of the company from the directors. Their first duty is to try to rescue it as a going concern.
'If that isn’t possible, they aim for a better result for creditors than liquidation would give. In practice that usually means a sale, either of the whole business or in parts. For staff and customers, stores normally keep trading while that happens, but the risk is that the business is broken up, with stronger stores sold and weaker ones closed.’
Who could buy the shops?
Owner Gordon Brothers rejected a takeover offer from Irish real estate firm Martin Property Group – despite management and unions arguing this was the best deal on the table.
This would have been for the whole business, including its brand and full store estate.
But now it seems like other major retailers, especially those with grand expansion plans, could pick up some shops from Poundland.
The owner of The Range, Homebase and Wilko – known as Britain’s ‘Del Boy Billionaire’ – is thought to be interested. Chris Dawson, 74, who runs CDS Superstores, acquired the Wilko brand out of administration in 2023.
Dawson got his nickname, the 'Del Boy billionaire', via the press as a reference to his yellow Lamborghini Urus, which has a personalised number plate 'DE11 BOY', a homage to the character Del Boy Trotter from the classic TV show Only Fools and Horses.
Dawson started his career as a market trader, before founding The Range and scaling it to a major high street chain. He has since acquired Wilko and Homebase out of administration.
Chris Dawson, 74, runs CDS Superstores, which owns The Range, Homebase and Wilko
Poundstretcher owner Fortress is also understood to be looking at buying shops. The rival discount retailer runs more than 300 shops in the UK.
Supermarket Lidl also hopes to be able to snap up some of its stores if the retailer fails to sell the whole company. The discounter is pushing ahead with a major expansion mission.
TG Jones owner is also understood to be interested in buying parts of the Poundland business.
The private equity group owns Britain's WH Smith shops, now known as TG Jones stores and previously bought ailing accessories chain Claire's, Hobbycraft and The Original Factory Shop.
All Claire's standalone shops in the UK and Ireland stopped trading earlier this year after its financial woes saw it fall into administration twice in a year.
Are shops open and will staff be paid?
Poundland shops are currently open and operating business as usual.
But Poundland's managing director Barry Williams wrote a letter to around 12,000, accusing the retailer’s owner of limiting the chain's access to funding.
This has effectively prevented bosses from making routine payments, with suppliers now worried they will not be paid on time this week, according to Sky News.
But sources close to the crisis talks insisted that this should not prevent staff from being paid at the end of the month.
Williams told staff: 'I'm disappointed to have to tell you that Gordon Brothers have given instructions that restricts our access to funds that we would, in normal circumstances expect to access fully under our existing loan agreement.'
Gordon Brothers are accused of breaching the terms of an asset-based lending facility by failing to submit a budget to the shareholders on time despite an agreed grace period – with the business now outperforming those forecasts, Sky News reported.
Julie Palmer, managing partner at real estate advisory group BTG, says that in this situation, ‘existing commitments such as payroll and supplier invoices can still be met from cash already available‘.
But bosses cannot ‘draw further funds to cover anything beyond that,’ she says, which poses a problem as retailers typically draw from these loans in the autumn to buy Christmas stock - before repaying from festive sales in December and January.
She added: ‘If a lender has concerns about longer-term viability, it may simply be unwilling to increase its exposure by funding that stock build, particularly when it can’t be sure who will own the business, or what shape it will be in, by the time the money needs to come back.
‘That leaves management with very little room to manoeuvre. It limits their ability to buy stock or take on new commitments, and puts directors in a difficult position, because they must be confident the company can meet its liabilities before taking on new ones. Once credit insurers pull back and suppliers start asking for payment up front, the squeeze tightens quickly.’

items.body:
Landsec, owner of one of the UK’s leading retail and hospitality portfolios, has welcomed Indetix-owned Bershka to Westgate Oxford as leading brands continue to invest in the destination.
The new store opened today (29 October, 2026), bringing one of Europe’s most recognisable youth fashion brands to Westgate Oxford. Popular with Gen Z, Bershka strengthens the destination’s appeal to a generation that is increasingly influencing how brands think about physical retail.
The signing further strengthens Landsec’s long-standing relationship with Inditex and reflects continued confidence from one of the world’s largest fashion groups, in Landsec’s retail destinations.
Bershka’s arrival also reflects continued demand from major international brands looking to grow within high-performing retail destinations. With more than 17 million visitors each year and a mix of local residents, students and tourists, Westgate Oxford continues to attract brands looking to connect with a broad customer base in the heart of one of the UK’s most visited cities.
The opening follows a series of recent new additions at Westgate Oxford, including Sephora and LEGO, whose new store attracted significant crowds on opening day. Together with Bershka’s arrival, these signings highlight the continued appeal of Westgate Oxford to leading international brands.
Pablo Sueiras, head of retail & hospitality leasing at Landsec, said: “Bershka is a fantastic addition to Westgate Oxford and further reinforces the destination’s position as a leading retail and leisure destination. As retailers focus investment on locations that can deliver reach, engagement and growth, Westgate Oxford continues to attract sought-after brands and concepts. With a loyal Gen Z customer base, Bershka brings a fresh dimension to our fashion offer and enhances the appeal of the destination for both new and existing visitors.”

Frasers Plus Braehead has secured another major market first, with Bath & Body Works set to open its first standalone store in Scotland at the retail and leisure destination this winter.
Opening ahead of Christmas, the new store, spanning more than 2,000 sq ft, will add a significant new gifting offer to the destination at the busiest time in the retail calendar. Bath & Body Works’ established appeal across fragrance, beauty and seasonal gifting will give shoppers another compelling reason to visit Frasers Plus Braehead.
The signing enhances Frasers Plus Braehead’s beauty and lifestyle line-up, joining Rituals, Boots, LUSH, M&S and TK Maxx, alongside Scotland’s largest Superdrug store. With White Stuff also due to open shortly, the destination continues to build a varied brand mix for shoppers across the region.
The signing follows the recent opening of SuperPark’s first UK location at Braehead, further reinforcing the destination’s appeal to leading national and international brands.
Rachel Scott, head of leasing at Global Mutual, commented: “Bath & Body Works’ decision to select Frasers Plus Braehead for its first standalone Scottish store is a significant endorsement of the destination’s regional reach and the momentum behind our evolving offer.
“Bath & Body Works will broaden our beauty offer across body care, home fragrance and gifting, while giving shoppers access to the full standalone store experience. Opening ahead of Christmas, it will introduce a strong new gifting proposition that complements the wider destination at a key trading moment.”
A spokesperson from Bath & Body Works, said: “Opening our first standalone Scottish store is an important milestone for Bath & Body Works, and Frasers Plus Braehead is the ideal location for this next step in our growth.
“The destination’s strong regional draw and impressive mix of leading retail brands made it a natural choice for our debut. We look forward to bringing the full Bath & Body Works experience to Braehead and building meaningful relationships with customers across Scotland.”
Bath & Body Works is due to open at Frasers Plus Braehead in winter 2026. For more information about Frasers Plus Braehead visit their website here: https://frasersplusbraehead.co.uk/

PATRÓN EL ALTO, the exceptionally aged tequila, is passionately crafted from the highest-quality 100% Blue Weber Agave that is cultivated in the highest parts of Jalisco, Mexico, where the sweetest agave grows. Best enjoyed neat or on the rocks, the unique blend of PATRÓN Extra Añejo, Añejo and Reposado results in a unique high-end tequila that beckons to be savored.
- Savor the soft, sweet aromatic notes of agave, dried fruit and toasted wood when you pour a glass of PATRÓN EL ALTO. The light gold, captivatingly bright colour is a hint of what is to come. Delightfully bright flavours emerge, tasting of apricots, vanilla, almonds and cooked agave. PATRÓN EL ALTO is impressively smooth, subtly sweet and best enjoyed neat or on the rocks.
- We grow the highest-quality 100% Blue Weber Agave in the highest parts of the Atotonilco El Alto region in Jalisco, Mexico, that yields the sweetest agaves and which inspired the name for PATRÓN EL ALTO. After we harvest the sweet agave, we ground it with ancient volcanic stone, bake it for days in clay ovens and masterfully age it.
- PATRÓN EL ALTO is composed of PATRÓN Extra Añejo—aged for four years—blended with exceptional PATRÓN Añejo and Reposado tequilas, resulting in a uniquely innovative, beautifully crafted expression of bold and sweet flavors.
- PATRÓN tequila is widely available in the UK, with El Alto bottles available to purchase from retailers including Selfridges and the brand’s Amazon.com storefront. Link here.
- Reposado means “rested” in Spanish, and it signifies the period when the tequila ages in oak barrels to develop its exquisitely smooth character. PATRÓN Reposado is aged at least four months in oak barrels at Hacienda PATRÓN in Mexico, developing a complex yet balanced ultra-premium flavour profile that works beautifully in cocktails and long drinks, from a refreshing PATRÓN Paloma to a Spicy Margarita.
- As the tequila ages, it absorbs the rich characteristics of the wood from the barrels, which imparts unique depth and smoothness to this world-famous tequila.
- Only the highest-quality ingredients are used to craft this spirit, which maintains the roasted agave flavours unique to PATRÓN mingled in perfect harmony with hints of light oak and vanilla.
- Perfect to sip neat or in a cocktail, the aging process turns the liquid to a marvellous shade of light amber gold, imbuing it with a light oaky flavour alongside big, cooked agave notes.
- PATRÓN tequila is widely available in the UK, with 70cl PATRÓN Reposado bottles found at major supermarkets and Amazon.com.
- The world’s first super-premium silver tequila, handcrafted from the finest 100% Blue Weber Agave, PATRÓN Silver is perfect for sipping or mixing in a wide range of cocktails, including the classic PATRÓN Margarita.
- PATRÓN Silver captures the unaged spirit of agave, revealing its sweet and smooth flavour while offering a crisp, clean taste. Made using a handcrafted distillation process unique to PATRÓN, this clear spirit is produced with only three natural, high quality ingredients—100% Blue Weber Agave, yeast and water.
- Made with the finest 100% Blue Weber Agave and handcrafted using time-honoured traditional methods, PATRÓN Silver is a testament to authentic Mexican heritage and to the spirit of the agave plant.
- PATRÓN tequila is widely available in the UK, with 70cl PATRÓN Silver bottles found at major supermarkets and Amazon.com.
- PATRÓN Miniatures bring the brand’s premium tequila range into a convenient 5cl format, available across PATRÓN Silver, Reposado and El Alto.
- PATRÓN Silver is a clear, crisp and smooth tequila made from 100% Blue Weber Agave, with a clean profile that makes it ideal for sipping or mixing into cocktails.
- PATRÓN Reposado is aged for at least four months in oak barrels, developing a smooth, rounded character with notes of roasted agave, light oak and vanilla.
- PATRÓN El Alto is an exceptionally aged expression combining PATRÓN Extra Añejo, Añejo and Reposado tequilas, creating a rich and complex profile with notes of agave, dried fruit, toasted wood, apricot, vanilla and almond.

items.body:
Very, the online retailer operated by The Very Group, has unveiled a price commitment which guarantees the price customers pay on Black Friday offers will always be the cheapest, even if the same item is reduced further during its Black Friday event.
The Price Promise covers eligible Black Friday discounted products across all categories, from fashion, electrical and toys to home, beauty and sports.
Eligible Black Friday purchases will be protected against subsequent Very price reductions throughout the entire Black Friday event, from 28 October to 4 December.
Robbie Feather, chief executive officer, The Very Group, said: “Our Price Promise is all about giving customers greater confidence that they’re getting the best deal. For Black Friday, we’re going even further.
“One of the biggest decisions customers face during Black Friday is deciding whether to buy now or wait to see if prices fall even further.
“Our Price Promise removes that uncertainty. Customers can shop our deals as soon as they see them, safe in the knowledge that if we reduce the price of an eligible product later in the event, they won’t miss out.”
Very’s Black Friday commitment covers eligible Black Friday discounted lines across all categories, and protects the price customers pay against subsequent price reductions by Very for the duration of the Black Friday event.
If an eligible product bought during the Black Friday event is later reduced by Very before 4 December 2026, customers can contact Very Customer Services by that date and, subject to the terms of the promise, claim back the difference.
Alongside the Black Friday price promise, Very is also offering customers an everyday price promise across thousands of products within its electrical and toys categories.

items.body:
Leading sports nutrition brand Warrior® has launched a new line of accessible protein, tapping into growing mainstream demand for affordable, everyday protein.
Now officially available in Asda stores nationwide, Warrior Serious Protein offers consumers a convenient way to incorporate more protein into their daily routines, for just £12.50 per 500g tub.
Available in three classic flavours – Chocolate, Strawberry and Vanilla Milkshake – Serious Protein delivers 24g of protein, 110 calories and just 0.3g of fat per 30g. Designed for everyday use, it can be enjoyed in post-workout shakes, with breakfast or as an afternoon protein top-up.
Each tub contains 16 servings, and the new innovative formula combines soy protein isolate, skimmed milk powder, casein and glutamine peptides, with no added sugar. It is also suitable for vegetarians.
The launch comes amidst rising whey protein prices alongside growing consumer demand for protein products. Increasing interest in fitness and wellness, combined with greater awareness of the importance of maintaining muscle mass among GLP-1 users, are fuelling this growth.
Kieran Fisher, founder and CEO of Warrior®, said “We wanted to create a protein powder that delivers on the fundamentals consumers are looking for, which is high protein content, great-tasting flavours and an accessible price point.
“There’s no avoiding the fact that the cost of whey has increased globally due to high demand, so we’ve looked at how we can offer consumers an accessible alternative without compromising on the things that matter.
“Serious Protein is designed to give more people an affordable way to hit their protein goals. It also sits alongside our bestselling range of whey protein tubs and bars, giving consumers and our retail partners even more choice as demand for protein shows no sign of slowing down.”
Serious Protein is made in Warrior’s own BRCGS certified factory in Trafford Park, Manchester, where the brand has been producing sports nutrition since 2008.
Warrior Serious Protein is available now in Asda stores nationwide, Amazon and at www.teamwarrior.com.

items.title: Union in plea to save Poundland from administration, with 12,000 jobs at risk
items.summary: Owner Gordon Brothers files notice of intent to begin process after rejecting management-backed rescue bid Business live – latest updates The shop workers’ union Usdaw has urged Poundland’s owners to reconsider a decision to prepare the budget chain for administration, putting up to 12,000 jobs at risk. Gordon Brothers filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators to Poundland at the high court on Thursday, with the advisory firm AlixPartners lined up to run the process. Continue reading...
items.body:
The shop workers’ union Usdaw has urged Poundland’s owners to reconsider a decision to prepare the budget chain for administration, putting up to 12,000 jobs at risk.
Gordon Brothers filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators to Poundland at the high court on Thursday, with the advisory firm AlixPartners lined up to run the process.
The legal measure protects Poundland from the demands of creditors for 10 days while a solution to its problems is sought.
Gordon Brothers previously rejected a management-backed rescue bid for the discount chain, which operates 600 stores, including Dealz outlets in Ireland. It bought the struggling chain for a nominal £1 from its previous owner, the European retail group Pepco, in June 2025.
Only one bidder, Martin Property Group, a Northern Irish family-owned company, was interested in buying the entire chain and working with the existing management, led by Barry Williams, the chief executive.
Gordon Brothers is understood to believe that it can raise more from a breakup of Poundland than through the Martin offer, which was worth less than the £30m in debts that Gordon Brothers took on when it bought the chain.
The threat of administration leaves thousands of shop workers facing uncertainty in the run-up to Christmas. Rival cut-price retailers, including Poundstretcher, The Range and B&M, have reportedly expressed an interest in taking on some Poundland stores.
Bally Auluk, national officer of the Union of Shop, Distributive and Allied Workers, said: “It has been an incredibly distressing week for Poundland staff who have had to watch from the sidelines as a multibillion-pound company jeopardises their livelihoods as it tries to extract £30m from a business it bought for £1.
“We are urging Gordon Brothers to reconsider and to prioritise a unified buyer who will protect the livelihoods of [more than] 11,000 people.”
Williams wrote to workers this week saying the rejection of the bid from Martin Property Group was “unexpected, unwanted and wholly avoidable”.
The board of Poundland said on Thursday: “We recognise any sale process creates uncertainty and particularly when set against a challenging UK economic environment.”
The board said the notice of the intention to appoint administrators had been filed “in order to bring stability” as “despite enormous efforts it has not been possible to identify an acceptable offer for the business as a whole”. Poundland would be “working closely with our advisors to identify and deliver the best possible outcome”.
Gordon Brothers hired the advisory company Alvarez & Marsal in August to oversee a sale of the business at a reported price of £30m, fuelling fears of a breakup, despite improved trading.
Poundland, founded with one store in Burton upon Trent in 1990, was the first UK-wide chain based on a single price. However, it now offers a broader range of price points and goods in a similar way to its rival Poundstretcher, which was founded in 1981.
Rising costs and heavy competition from chains such as Savers, Home Bargains and B&M, as well as from the major supermarkets, have meant pound shop chains have been gradually disappearing.
Poundworld closed its 350 stores in 2018, and Poundland bought its rival 99p Stores in 2015. Poundland then closed about 200 of its then 800 UK stores in a restructuring last year.
In 2020, Poundstretcher was due to close about half its then 270 stores in a rescue restructure but it now has more than 300 outlets after being bought by Majestic Wine’s owner, Fortress, in 2024.
The board of Poundland said the latest sale process for Poundland had attracted offers from several established retailers “which collectively cover a significant part of the business” and that “offer the best available prospects for shareholders, creditors and to preserve jobs”.
Five initially interested parties include the US company Fortress, which is thought to want to take fewer than half of Poundland’s stores to add to its existing chain.
CDS, owner of The Range, and B&M are understood to be considering a bid for at least some stores.

The Saracens forward has penned a two-year agreement to become an athlete ambassador for the wellness brand, which makes drinks supplements. The lock joins actor Hugh Jackman, racing driver Sir Lewis Hamilton and sprinter [...]
items.body:
England captain Itoje lands Snoop Dogg-linked sponsorship deal
England captain Maro Itoje has signed a deal with Swansea City sponsor AG1 ahead of next month’s Nations Championship at Twickenham.
The Saracens forward has penned a two-year agreement to become an athlete ambassador for the wellness brand, which makes drinks supplements.
The lock joins actor Hugh Jackman, racing driver Sir Lewis Hamilton and sprinter Allyson Felix within the AG1 roster as England prepare for a month of international rugby in which they will face New Zealand, Japan and Australia before a finals weekend at Allianz Stadium in London.
AG1 this summer became the front-of-shirt sponsor of Championship high-flyers Swansea City, whose eclectic ownership consortium includes minority holdings for rapper Snoop Dogg, lifestyle guru Martha Stewart and footballer Luka Modric.
The wellness brand offers a green health powder, mixed with water, as its primary product, with the Swansea deal AG1’s first venture in football.
The Chris Ashenden-founded brand, which in 2022 raised $115m in a funding round that valued AG1 at $1.2bn, also has agreements with the wider England Rugby organisation.
Itoje on board
Tim Harrington of AG1 said: “Maro embodies exactly what we look for in a partner – someone who lives our product, not just endorses it. His story, on and off the pitch, is proof that consistency compounds. We’re proud to help him tell it.”
Their sponsorship of Swansea City bucked a trend of shirts being fronted by gambling organisations following a voluntary ban of the sector in the same advertising space across the Premier League.
“The partnership will roll out across further film,” a statement read, “including the brand’s ‘Morning Person’ format ft. Maro – as well as longform press, podcast content and a UK event programme in the months ahead, with further details to follow.”
England’s autumn campaign will likely see Itoje extend his number of caps beyond the 102 he currently has.
